# Ask LLM

> Second opinions for coding agents. Get a second opinion on your code or plan, inside your coding assistant, using the model subscriptions you already have.

For individual developers and small teams who already use a coding assistant and another model subscription. Review changes or challenge a plan without API keys, copy-paste, or leaving the session.

Install on Linux or macOS with Node.js 24+, then select your host and confirm the preview:

```bash
npm i -g @ask-llm/mcp && ask-llm setup
```

Install and sign in to the provider separately. Then ask: “Ask Codex to review my staged changes for bugs and missing error handling.” Choose a reviewer from a different vendor. Calls consume account quota or billing; Grok's metered API is explicit. Local Ollama models are supported. Antigravity refuses by default and opt-in has no read-only guarantee. Ask LLM sends no telemetry. Agreement between models is not proof of correctness.

## Start

### Install

Source: https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/start/install.html

Get a second opinion on your code or plan, inside your coding assistant, using the model subscriptions you already have.

## Before you start

Use Node.js 24+ on Linux or macOS. Before your first review, both your coding assistant (for example Claude Code) and the provider you will consult (for example Codex) must be installed and signed in. Ask LLM configures their connection; it does not install providers or sign you in. If a provider CLI such as Codex has never been signed in on this machine, sign in first and rerun setup. See [authentication](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/operation/authentication) if either account is not ready.

## Install and connect

See the install command above; select your host, inspect the preview, and confirm.

Setup discovers hosts separately from providers and asks you to confirm each detected host and workflow. Review the command or file preview, confirm your assistant's registration and workflows, and decline the others. Setup works at user scope, preserves unrelated entries, and prints backup locations and restart instructions. Pairing remains off.

Follow any manual guidance in the output before continuing. Codex registration is always a manual step: setup installs the Codex workflows and prints the exact `codex mcp add ask-llm -- <path>` command, but does not run it, because Codex's server list omits persisted settings and can include project overrides. Check `~/.codex/config.toml` and project configuration for an existing `ask-llm` entry, then run the printed command. Antigravity needs the printed workflow-copy step. OpenCode registration is tested with fixtures only. See [host compatibility](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/compatibility/hosts) and [migration](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/reference/migration).

Start a new session in your project or restart your assistant, then [ask for your first review](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/start/first-review).

## Preview without changing anything

```bash
ask-llm setup --dry-run
```

To target just one assistant, use `ask-llm setup --host claude` (or another [host ID](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/reference/cli#host-ids)). Running setup again preserves compatible registrations and refreshes changed workflows.

If no supported assistant is found, use [manual configuration](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/advanced/manual-configuration). If setup fails, run `ask-llm doctor` and use [troubleshooting](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/resources/troubleshooting).

### First review

Source: https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/start/first-review.html

Before your first review, both your coding assistant (for example Claude Code) and the provider you will consult (for example Codex) must be installed and signed in. Ask LLM configures the connection; it does not install providers or sign you in. If a provider CLI such as Codex has never been signed in on this machine, sign in first and rerun `ask-llm setup`.

Open a project with a small staged change. With both Claude Code and Codex signed in, ask in Claude Code:

```text
Ask Codex to review my staged changes for bugs and missing error handling. Check each finding against the source before proposing fixes.
```

If Codex is your host, ask Claude instead. You can name any [provider](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/start/install#before-you-start) you have authenticated; choose a different vendor from the model writing the code.

A successful response identifies the reviewer and model and cites code supporting its findings, or says it found none. Your assistant stays responsible for editing. Review the evidence and decide which fixes to apply; agreement between models is not proof of correctness.

If you get a missing-tool or authentication error, run `ask-llm doctor` in your terminal, follow its remediation for your selected assistant and reviewer, and restart the host. Warnings about providers you do not use do not require installing them or adding API keys. [Troubleshooting](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/resources/troubleshooting) covers common failures. Registration alone does not prove a provider can answer.

Next, [review a larger change](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/workflows/review-changes) or [challenge a plan](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/workflows/challenge-plan).

### Upgrade and remove

Source: https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/start/upgrade-remove.html

## Upgrade

Repeat the install line from [Install](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/start/install), then restart the host. Setup preserves compatible registrations and refreshes changed workflows. It previews replacements for earlier registrations and leaves customised entries with guidance; see [migration](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/reference/migration).

## Remove registrations

```bash
ask-llm remove
```

Inspect the preview and confirm. MCP removal deletes only registrations whose command resolves to this installation's server. Codex receives manual guidance when ownership cannot be verified. Removal does not restore replaced or retired entries.

Pi removal runs `pi remove` for this installed package's local entry after confirmation; foreign and legacy npm entries and local entries with custom filters stay in place. The Claude Code plugin and portable skills remain installed. Removal prints scoped cleanup commands with concrete names only for installed portable skills whose complete contents match this package. Modified or unverified copies receive no command. A present user-scoped Claude Code plugin is reported without an uninstall command because setup keeps no ownership record. Shared skill removal can affect several hosts reading the same folder. User-owned pairing logs, cache and consent remain until you explicitly remove or revoke them.

If Pi removal reports a failed or manual step with a `pi remove` command, inspect the reported reason before running it manually. Earlier Pi npm installations remain unchanged and need the [migration guidance](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/reference/migration).

After removing registrations and any workflows you no longer want, uninstall the global installation with npm. The exact package name is in the [install line](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/start/install). Backups remain beside the host's config; they may contain credentials and retain the original file permissions (or owner-only permissions if those could not be read).


## Workflows

### Review changes

Source: https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/workflows/review-changes.html

Start with a bounded diff and a specific review question:

```text
Ask Codex to review the staged changes for security issues, performance, and missing error handling.
```

Give the reviewer the change's purpose and constraints. Ask your assistant to include the diff and relevant surrounding code, then check each finding at the cited file and line. The reviewer reads; your assistant applies the changes you accept.

## Review workflow

The portable `ask-llm-review` workflow gathers staged and unstaged changes, reads project conventions, consults Codex and filters findings by confidence. Claude Code retains `/codex-review`; Pi uses `/skill:ask-llm-review`. Other hosts expose portable names through their skills menu. See [host compatibility](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/compatibility/hosts).

For independent parallel review, use `ask-llm-multi-review`. The assistant validates candidate findings against source and separates supported findings, false positives and claims requiring runtime evidence. Antigravity is skipped unless its execution gate is explicitly enabled; that opt-in has no read-only guarantee. Partial results disclose failed providers.

## Keep the review useful

Use a narrow scope, include domain invariants, and request actionable issues rather than style preferences. Large diffs can take several minutes and consume substantial quota; split them by concern when possible. Agreement between models is not proof of correctness. Use tests for claims about runtime behavior.

For local analysis, ask Ollama to review the relevant code. For continuing feedback as you edit, see [pair review](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/advanced/codex-pair), which is off until you opt in. The [workflow catalogue](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/reference/skills) describes provider-specific variants.

### Challenge a plan

Source: https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/workflows/challenge-plan.html

Share the proposal, constraints and relevant code with a reviewer from another vendor:

```text
Ask Claude to challenge this plan before we implement it. What assumptions could fail, what evidence is missing, and what simpler alternative would fit our constraints?
```

Use Claude from a host other than Claude Code; ask Codex or another authenticated provider when working in Claude Code. Name the constraints that would make a recommendation unusable: migration compatibility, latency, budget, data boundaries or team size.

Ask the reviewer to distinguish observed facts from assumptions. Your assistant should validate claims against source or primary documentation before changing the plan. The number of models agreeing does not establish correctness.

For several independent answers without synthesis, [compare answers](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/workflows/compare-answers). For research followed by an attributed synthesis, [brainstorm](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/workflows/brainstorm).

### Compare answers

Source: https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/workflows/compare-answers.html

Use the same bounded context for every reviewer:

```text
Ask Codex and Claude to review this API design. Show their raw answers side by side, without synthesis.
```

Use providers your host can consult; Claude is unavailable inside Claude Code. The `ask-llm-compare` workflow returns verbatim answers with attribution. Claude Code retains `/compare`; Pi uses `/skill:ask-llm-compare`. Tool-only hosts can ask their assistant to call `multi-llm` with the selected providers.




One provider failure does not erase the others' answers. Keep failures visible and attribute surviving insights only to providers that answered. Compare evidence and disagreements, not vote counts: agreement between models is not proof of correctness.

For a report that checks findings against the code, use [Review changes](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/workflows/review-changes). For research and synthesis, use [Brainstorm](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/workflows/brainstorm).

### Brainstorm

Source: https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/workflows/brainstorm.html

Ask for independent research followed by synthesis:

```text
Ask Codex and Grok to challenge our notification architecture. Separate evidence, assumptions, disagreements and recommended next steps.
```

The portable workflow is `ask-llm-brainstorm`; Claude Code retains `/brainstorm` and Pi uses `/skill:ask-llm-brainstorm`. The host follows its own adapter and should not claim Claude-only subagents or hooks on another host. Each participant consumes its own account quota; explicitly choose metered routes only when you intend that cost.

## Consult one exact Codex model

```text
/brainstorm --external-only --no-fallback codex@codex-cli:gpt-6.2-astra "Review the trade-offs of this queue design"
/skill:ask-llm-brainstorm --external-only codex@codex-cli:gpt-6.2-astra "Review this queue design"
```

`--external-only` accepts one `codex@codex-cli:<exact-model-id>` participant and implies `--no-fallback`. The current host prepares the context and relays one read-only Codex consultation at high reasoning effort. The result identifies the transport, selected model and configured effort. A rejection on the named model ends the run with that error. The result contains only the external contribution, with no coordinator view or consensus.

Update the skill and tool together. Claude Code and other MCP hosts prefer a compatible `ask-codex` leaf, then a compatible unified `ask-llm` with Codex selected. When neither is exposed, hosts that permit local CLI use can disclose and make one direct Codex CLI call. Pi uses its native `ask-llm`. A tool must advertise `noFallback`; when only stale tools are exposed, upgrade and restart the host before running the command.

## Run a panel

Send a topic to an explicit multi-model panel, ground it with independent Claude Opus research, then synthesize the findings. Provider, harness, requested catalog ID, independently observed served model (direct xAI API / Grok CLI only; a disclosed same-product alias/snapshot stays eligible), and Cursor's optional reported display label remain separate. Cursor Agent and Codex CLI echo the requested ID, so those attributions are selected-only and unverifiable rather than an actual model. The coordinator agent runs:

1. **Phase 3B: Claude Opus research.** Claude reads actual files, traces real code paths, fetches referenced docs, and forms findings tagged Verified or Inferred. In standard mode Claude is a participant. In the exact Grok + Sol mode it is a non-voting evidence verifier, so the requested panel remains exactly two models.
2. **Phase 3A: External dispatch.** A single foreground blocking Bash call sends the topic to each requested external provider in parallel and waits for all of them. Up to 10 minutes total (Bash tool max). It's a foreground blocking call, not a background-job dispatch, because sub-agents can't own processes that outlive their turn.
3. **Phase 4: Synthesis.** Combines Claude's findings with the external responses:

- Consensus points (where multiple participants agree; Claude verified + external = highest confidence)
- Unique insights (findings from only one participant)
- Contradictions (verified findings outrank inferred ones)
- Actionable recommendations (prioritized by impact and confidence)

```text
# Default Claude Code panel (Antigravity + Codex + Claude Opus)
/ask-llm-brainstorm Should we use a monorepo or polyrepo for this project?

# Custom external providers
/ask-llm-brainstorm gemini,codex,ollama Review this authentication approach

# Standard Claude Code panel with one Codex attempt; Claude still contributes
/ask-llm-brainstorm --no-fallback codex Compare these two cache policies

# Architect panel: exactly Grok + GPT-6 Sol via Cursor Agent; Gemini excluded
/ask-llm-brainstorm grok@cursor-agent:grok-4.7-high,codex@cursor-agent:gpt-6.2-sol-high "review this architecture"

# Explicit direct-Grok alternative; never pivots away from Grok Build
/ask-llm-brainstorm grok@grok-cli:grok-4.7,codex@cursor-agent:gpt-6.2-sol-high "review this architecture"
```

**Default external providers:** `antigravity,codex` (avoids unnecessary Ollama calls). Antigravity follows the [execution gate](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/providers/antigravity). Compatible bare provider lists remain supported. For predictable routing use `provider@harness:exact-model-id`; the preferred Grok path is Cursor Agent. A list is either all bare names or all routed specs—mixing them (for example `grok@cursor-agent:grok-4.7-high,antigravity`) is refused before any provider is called, with no rerouting or substitution; generalized mixed panels are deferred to a future ADR. Exact IDs come from the selected harness catalog (`agent --list-models`, `grok models`, or xAI `/v1/models`) and are never translated between catalogs.

The Cursor `gpt-6.2-sol-high` example follows the `<codex-slug>-high` naming but is unverified; confirm the exact ID with `agent --list-models` before use.

The architect panel invokes only the two listed Cursor participants: `provider: "grok"` with `model: "grok-4.7-high"`, and `provider: "codex"` with `model: "gpt-6.2-sol-high"`. It never calls Gemini or Cursor `Auto`. If registration, authentication, model availability, or route support fails for either participant, the result is **partial** and surviving insights are attributed only to the model that answered—never called two-model consensus. Claude's evidence can verify claims but cannot supply the missing vote.

The `grok-cli` form is supported only when the installed official Grok Build exposes Ask LLM's required headless JSON/read-only contract. A direct-route failure is terminal for that participant; there is no silent pivot among Cursor Agent, Grok CLI, or xAI API.

`--no-fallback` by itself controls the Codex second-model attempt for a Claude Code panel with bare Codex or an exact Grok + Sol panel on a compatible route. An exact Codex request through Cursor Agent already makes one dispatch. Portable bare-list batch tools cannot enforce this flag. Other providers keep their own retry policies.

Agreement between models is not proof of correctness. Check the evidence behind the synthesis, and keep dissent and skipped participants in the final report.


## Compatibility

### Hosts

Source: https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/compatibility/hosts.html

A host is the coding assistant you work in. A provider is the model you consult. The matrix below is kept equal to the canonical [HOST-PARITY matrix](https://github.com/Lykhoyda/ask-llm/blob/main/docs/HOST-PARITY.md); `ask-llm doctor` prints the rows for installed hosts.



| | Claude Code | Codex | Cursor | Antigravity | Grok Build | Gemini | Pi | Claude Desktop | OpenCode |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| tools | MCP: ask-llm, multi-llm, ask-cursor-agent, ping, get-usage-stats, diagnose | MCP: ask-llm, multi-llm, ask-cursor-agent, ping, get-usage-stats, diagnose | MCP: ask-llm, multi-llm, ask-cursor-agent, ping, get-usage-stats, diagnose | MCP: ask-llm, multi-llm, ask-cursor-agent, ping, get-usage-stats, diagnose | MCP: ask-llm, multi-llm, ask-cursor-agent, ping, get-usage-stats, diagnose | MCP: ask-llm, multi-llm, ask-cursor-agent, ping, get-usage-stats, diagnose | native ask-llm, multi-llm, ask-cursor-agent with the MCP input schemas; ask-codex-write for file writing; ask-codex, ask-gemini, ask-grok, ask-ollama, ask-antigravity, ask-multi as deprecated aliases | MCP: ask-llm, multi-llm, ask-cursor-agent, ping, get-usage-stats, diagnose | MCP: ask-llm, multi-llm, ask-cursor-agent, ping, get-usage-stats, diagnose |
| skills | the Claude plugin, installed by `ask-llm setup` | shared skills folder `~/.agents/skills`, filled by `ask-llm setup` | shared skills folder `~/.agents/skills`, filled by `ask-llm setup` | `~/.gemini/config/skills`; `ask-llm setup` prints the copy command | `~/.grok/skills`, filled by `ask-llm setup` | shared skills folder `~/.agents/skills`, filled by `ask-llm setup` | shared skills folder `~/.agents/skills`, filled by `ask-llm setup` | none (tools only) | shared skills folder `~/.agents/skills`, filled by `ask-llm setup` |
| options | every `ask-llm` option reaches the executor unchanged; provider enums list providers detected at start, falling back to all eligible providers after exclusions when none are detected | every `ask-llm` option reaches the executor unchanged; provider enums list providers detected at start, falling back to all eligible providers after exclusions when none are detected | every `ask-llm` option reaches the executor unchanged; provider enums list providers detected at start, falling back to all eligible providers after exclusions when none are detected | every `ask-llm` option reaches the executor unchanged; provider enums list providers detected at start, falling back to all eligible providers after exclusions when none are detected | every `ask-llm` option reaches the executor unchanged; provider enums list providers detected at start, falling back to all eligible providers after exclusions when none are detected | every `ask-llm` option reaches the executor unchanged; provider enums list providers detected at start, falling back to all eligible providers after exclusions when none are detected | every `ask-llm` option reaches the executor unchanged; provider enums list providers detected at start, falling back to all eligible providers after exclusions when none are detected | every `ask-llm` option reaches the executor unchanged; provider enums list providers detected at start, falling back to all eligible providers after exclusions when none are detected | every `ask-llm` option reaches the executor unchanged; provider enums list providers detected at start, falling back to all eligible providers after exclusions when none are detected |
| diagnostics | `diagnose` tool and `ask-llm doctor` | `diagnose` tool and `ask-llm doctor` | `diagnose` tool and `ask-llm doctor` | `diagnose` tool and `ask-llm doctor` | `diagnose` tool and `ask-llm doctor` | `diagnose` tool and `ask-llm doctor` | `ask-llm doctor` (no `diagnose` tool) | `diagnose` tool and `ask-llm doctor` | `diagnose` tool and `ask-llm doctor` |
| pairing | per-edit codex-pair hooks from the plugin, off until `/codex-pair` consent | on demand through the `ask-llm-codex-pair` skill; no per-edit review | on demand through the `ask-llm-codex-pair` skill; no per-edit review | on demand through the `ask-llm-codex-pair` skill; no per-edit review | per-edit pair hook by manual registration; Codex default or opt-in Claude; off without the marker | on demand through the `ask-llm-codex-pair` skill; no per-edit review | per-edit Codex or Claude advisory review with project trust, a marker and reviewer-specific `/codex-pair` consent | none | on demand through the `ask-llm-codex-pair` skill; no per-edit review |
| subagents | isolated reviewer agents from the plugin | none; reviews run inline | none; reviews run inline | none; reviews run inline | none; reviews run inline | none; reviews run inline | none; reviews run inline | none | none; reviews run inline |
| Stop gate | blocks the turn on a HIGH codex-pair finding only with `blockOn: HIGH` | none | none | none | none | none | none; codex-pair findings are non-blocking | none | none |


## MCP protocol compatibility

Every Ask LLM stdio server accepts both the existing 2025 MCP protocol and [revision 2026-07-28](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/versioning). The client selects the protocol form; existing registrations continue to work without configuration changes. Tool names, annotations, schemas, structured responses, progress notifications, and session usage remain the same across both forms.

## Setup limits

Claude Desktop is tools only. Antigravity needs the workflow-copy step printed by setup. Codex registration is a manual step: setup installs the workflows and prints the `codex mcp add` command without running it; inspect user and project configuration, including filters, before you run it. OpenCode registration is tested with fixtures only. See [Migration](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/reference/migration) when setup leaves an earlier entry unchanged.

## Codex

After manual registration, merge `tool_timeout_sec = 2460` into the existing `[mcp_servers.ask-llm]` table in `~/.codex/config.toml` (or `$CODEX_HOME/config.toml`). Setup prints this setting without writing it. It covers the largest default per-attempt limit × three attempts + 60 seconds of overhead. If timeout environment variables raise the per-attempt limits, increase this host setting using the [Codex timeout formula](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/advanced/manual-configuration#codex-tool-timeout), then start a new Codex session.

## Claude Code

Claude Code has isolated reviewer agents and hooks. Only its opt-in `blockOn: HIGH` Stop gate can block a turn on pair findings; other hosts do not claim that gate. [Claude Code host notes](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/compatibility/claude-code) include the hooks and agents reference.

## Cursor

Cursor runs consent-gated pairing on demand, with exact provider/model options. It does not run Claude Code hooks. See [Cursor host notes](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/compatibility/cursor).

## Pi

Pi 0.83.0+ has native tools and per-edit pairing, gated by marker, project trust and user-owned consent. Findings do not block turns. One-shot print mode does not support asynchronous pairing. See [Pi host notes](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/compatibility/pi).

## Other hosts

Portable reviews, comparisons and brainstorming run inline where isolated subagents are unavailable. Tool prefixes and skill syntax belong to each host. The logical schemas and provider options are shared; provider-specific limits are described in each provider reference. Clients outside this matrix can use [manual configuration](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/advanced/manual-configuration), without a claim of automatic setup support.

### Claude Code host notes

Source: https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/compatibility/claude-code.html

Follow [Install](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/start/install), then start a new Claude Code session. Setup connects the server and installs the Claude Code workflows through the host's marketplace. This is an implementation detail of setup, not a separate onboarding step. Pairing remains off until you opt in.

Reviews, plan critique, comparisons and brainstorming use the same portable workflow contracts as other hosts. Claude Code can also launch isolated reviewers and run per-edit hooks. See [Review changes](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/workflows/review-changes), [workflow names](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/reference/skills), and the [host matrix](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/compatibility/hosts).

## Connection details

The Claude Code plugin itself still ships only the Codex MCP registration used by review and pairing commands. It starts the Codex server with `node` from the plugin's own `@ask-llm/mcp` release, pinned to the plugin version, as a single process per session. A plugin installed from the repository has no build of its own, so on its first start it installs that exact release once into `~/.cache/ask-llm/servers` (`$XDG_CACHE_HOME/ask-llm/servers` when set, or `ASK_LLM_SERVER_CACHE`); later starts use that copy without contacting npm. If the release cannot be installed, the server reports the manual install command and does not start, and the workflows below use their disclosed fallback. Fully restart Claude Code after installation or upgrade, then run `/mcp`; `plugin:ask-llm:codex` should be connected and expose the exact `ask-codex` capability. Plugin agents and skills prefer that bundled `ask-codex` leaf, then a fully pinned unified `ask-llm` call (`provider: "codex"` plus model and Codex options), then the disclosed `codex exec` fallback.

## Hooks

This page is Claude Code-specific. Pi uses native extension lifecycle events instead of these scripts; see [Pi Host Support](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/compatibility/pi) for its `tool_result`, debounce, delivery, consent, and shutdown mapping.

Hooks are automated actions that trigger on specific Claude Code events. Every hook the Ask LLM plugin ships is part of the **codex-pair** continuous-review pipeline, so this page is the hook-mechanics reference; the feature itself, its setup, slash commands, cost, and Stop gate live on the dedicated [Codex Pair](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/advanced/codex-pair) page.

> **Looking for codex-pair?** Setup, the `/codex-pair` slash commands, config knobs, cost characteristics, the opt-in Stop gate, and the "hook isn't firing" workaround all moved to [Codex Pair](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/advanced/codex-pair). This page only covers what hooks the plugin registers and how registration works.

### Hooks the plugin registers

All five hooks are dependency-free with zero workspace imports, required so they run from marketplace `git-subdir` installs that don't run `npm install`. Each self-gates on the `.codex-pair/context.md` marker file and stays silent (zero cost, zero Codex calls) unless a project opts in. Review transport, catch-up, and broker configuration are documented in [Codex Pair](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/advanced/codex-pair#the-hook-pipeline).

| Hook | Event | Action |
|------|-------|--------|
| `codex-pair-watch` | `PostToolUse` (Edit / Write / MultiEdit) | Debounced per-edit Codex review of the settled file state. See [Codex Pair → the hook pipeline](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/advanced/codex-pair#the-hook-pipeline) |
| `codex-pair-prompt-drain` | `UserPromptSubmit` | Drains queued codex-pair verdicts that finished mid-turn so they reach Claude without waiting for the next edit |
| `codex-pair-stop-gate` | `Stop` | See [catch-up review](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/advanced/codex-pair#catch-up-review) and [Stop gate behavior](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/advanced/codex-pair#stop-gate-opt-in) |
| `codex-pair-session` | `SessionStart` | See [the hook pipeline](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/advanced/codex-pair#the-hook-pipeline) |
| `codex-pair-session` | `SessionEnd` | Clears debounce state and manages broker teardown; see [Codex Pair](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/advanced/codex-pair) |

### How hook registration works

The plugin ships `hooks/hooks.json`, which Claude Code reads on plugin install. Each entry maps an event (`PostToolUse`, `Stop`, `SessionStart`, `SessionEnd`, `UserPromptSubmit`) to a `command` that invokes a script under `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/`. The `PostToolUse` entry additionally carries a `matcher` (`Edit|Write|MultiEdit`) so it only fires for edit-shaped tool calls.

Because the scripts have zero workspace imports, they run identically from a source checkout and from a marketplace `git-subdir` install (which never runs `npm install`). If a Claude Code install doesn't auto-invoke the plugin-declared `PostToolUse` hook, a project-local `.claude/settings.local.json` workaround registers the script directly; see [Codex Pair → the project-settings workaround](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/advanced/codex-pair#if-the-hook-isn-t-firing-automatically-the-project-settings-workaround-issue-74).

### Removed hooks

The plugin previously shipped two other hooks that have been removed:

- A `Stop` hook, removed because the `Stop` event fires per-turn rather than per-session, making it noisy and high-latency, and `git diff HEAD` excluded untracked files which silently dropped coverage on new-file sessions. See [Codex Pair](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/advanced/codex-pair#the-hook-pipeline) for the current Stop hook.
- A `PreToolUse` pre-commit Gemini-review hook, removed because per-file codex-pair review delivers higher-recall feedback continuously *during* editing rather than only at commit time, and the on-demand `/gemini-review` skill covers the explicit-review need.

Use the `/gemini-review` slash command for explicit on-demand pre-commit reviews instead, or the `/codex-review` skill for a precision-first PR-style review.

## Agents

Agents are specialized sub-processes that Claude Code dispatches to handle complex tasks. Each agent runs in an isolated context window, preventing review noise from polluting your main conversation.

### Review Agents

#### `fable-reviewer`

This native reviewer analyzes the current diff directly in an isolated context pinned to `fable`. It has read-only tools, verifies every candidate against the source, and reports only findings at 80% confidence or higher.

Invoke it with `/fable-review`.

#### `sol-reviewer`

This reviewer uses an isolated Opus coordinator to request `gpt-6.2-sol` explicitly at high reasoning, then validates Sol's findings against the source. Invoke it with `/sol-review`. It prefers any exact `ask-codex` leaf (including the plugin-bundled Codex server), otherwise a fully pinned unified `ask-llm` call (`provider: "codex"` plus model and Codex options), otherwise the disclosed `codex exec` fallback. An older unified schema that cannot honor those options is reported rather than stripped. A quota fallback to Terra is disclosed instead of being presented as a Sol result.

#### `astra-reviewer`

This reviewer follows the same transport ladder as `sol-reviewer` with an explicit `gpt-6.2-astra` pin at high reasoning. Invoke it with `/astra-review` for code changes or a named plan. A quota fallback is reported as a Terra result.

Provider-backed review agents use a 3-phase workflow with confidence-based filtering:

**Phase 1: Context Gathering**
- Read the project's `CLAUDE.md` for conventions
- Analyze the git diff (staged + unstaged)
- Identify affected files and their purpose

**Phase 2: Provider Consultation**
- Construct a targeted prompt with the diff and conventions
- Call the respective provider (Codex, Grok, Antigravity, Ollama, or Gemini)
- Parse the structured response

**Phase 3: Synthesis**
- Filter findings by confidence score (80%+ threshold)
- Group as **Critical** (90%+) or **Important** (80-89%)
- Discard low-confidence noise

#### `codex-reviewer`

Sends code changes to OpenAI Codex (GPT-6.2 Sol) for review. Automatic fallback to GPT-6.1 Terra on quota limits.

#### `antigravity-reviewer`

Sends code changes to Google's Antigravity CLI (`agy`) for review with explicit local opt-in. See the [Ask LLM route, Google's consumer-plan terms, and account checks](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/providers/antigravity).

#### `grok-reviewer`

Sends code changes to Grok through the selected xAI API or official Grok CLI harness. Exact model and harness attribution are preserved; failures never route to another model/provider. API data transfer and pricing are explicit.

#### `ollama-reviewer`

Sends code changes to a local Ollama model. All processing stays on your machine; no data leaves your network.

#### `gemini-reviewer`

Sends code changes to Gemini CLI for review with an [existing, eligible Gemini Code Assist Standard or Enterprise seat](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/providers/gemini).

### Brainstorm Agent

#### `brainstorm-coordinator`

The solo command `/brainstorm --external-only codex@codex-cli:gpt-6.2-astra <topic>` runs in the current conversation before the coordinator. The marketplace plugin's bundled `ask-codex` leaf supports the request when its schema advertises `noFallback`. A compatible unified `ask-llm` can also serve it, including when a separately installed split leaf is stale. After an upgrade, restart Claude Code and check the connected tools in `/mcp`.

Orchestrates multi-LLM brainstorming sessions with **Claude Opus as a first-class research participant** in standard mode. In the exact Grok + GPT-6 Sol mode (see [`/brainstorm`](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/reference/skills#brainstorm)) Claude's research is a non-voting evidence memo, the panel is exactly the two requested participants, and one participant failure makes the run partial rather than two-model consensus. The agent runs four phases sequentially within a single sub-agent turn:

**Phase 1: Context Gathering.** Identify the topic, gather diffs/files/conversation context referenced by it.

**Phase 2: Prompt Construction.** Build a structured prompt for the external providers (numbered points, pros/cons, deliverables).

**Phase 3B: Claude Opus Research (runs first).** Claude reads the actual artifacts referenced by the topic with `Read`/`Glob`/`Grep`, traces real code paths, uses `WebFetch`/`WebSearch` for any referenced external docs, and forms its own independent findings. Each finding is tagged **Verified** (backed by an actual file Read or fetched doc) or **Inferred** (reasoned from the topic description). This phase MUST complete before Phase 3A so Claude cannot anchor on external responses.

**Phase 3A: External Provider Dispatch (runs after 3B).** A SINGLE foreground blocking Bash call handles selected external providers via direct backgrounding (`cmd > out 2>&1 &`) plus per-PID `wait`, with `timeout: 600000` (10 min, the Bash tool maximum). The raw Antigravity participant follows the [execution gate](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/providers/antigravity). The exact Grok + Sol panel instead runs one foreground `ask-brainstorm-run` process that owns both concurrent routed participants. Background jobs are explicitly forbidden because sub-agents cannot own processes that outlive their turn; Codex at high reasoning effort gets SIGKILLed silently otherwise. Per-provider stdout AND stderr are captured so failures are loud.

**Phase 4: Synthesis.** Combines Claude's Phase 3B findings with the external responses:
   - **Consensus**: Where multiple participants agree (verified Claude + external = highest confidence)
   - **Unique insights**: Findings from only one participant
   - **Contradictions**: Verified findings outrank inferred ones in tie-breaking
   - **Recommendations**: Prioritized by impact and confidence

The `Participants Consulted` section lists each participant by provider, harness, and requested model or discloses why it was skipped (Claude Opus has a `(verified against real files: ...)` annotation; in exact mode it is marked non-voting and Gemini is listed as explicitly excluded). This agent is invoked by the `/brainstorm` and `/brainstorm-all` skills.

### Running Agents Directly

You can also invoke agents directly from Claude Code:

```text
Use the codex-reviewer agent to review my current changes
```

Or in automated workflows via the Agent tool with `subagent_type`.

### Cursor host notes

Source: https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/compatibility/cursor.html

Setup registers the user-scope connection and installs portable workflows into the skills folder. Follow [Install](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/start/install) and restart Cursor. The source adapter exposes two pair skills and their earlier-name pointers; it disables discovery of Claude-only agents and hooks. The repository root's `.cursor-plugin/marketplace.json` points Cursor at that adapter in `packages/llm-mcp` when the repository is added as a plugin source. See [manual configuration](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/advanced/manual-configuration) for project scope and [Migration](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/reference/migration) for earlier registrations.

## `/codex-pair` on Cursor

Apply the [portable writer applicability rule](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/advanced/codex-pair) before this adapter. When pairing is applicable, Cursor's `/codex-pair` is an on-demand iterative pair session. Cursor remains the editor; an authenticated Codex CLI is the explicit read-only reviewer. Both `model=<exact ID>` and `effort=low|medium|high|xhigh|max|ultra` are required: the adapter cannot safely infer environment defaults inside a separately spawned MCP server. If either is omitted, pairing stops before extra context is read or consent is requested. Before calling the provider it reports those exact choices, bounded files, relative include directories, quota/data boundary, and asks for consent.

The first Codex call (`ask-codex` when user-installed, otherwise the fully pinned unified `ask-llm` with `provider: "codex"`) passes `sessionId: ""` to create a persisted thread, `sandbox: "read-only"`, and may pass up to 32 safe relative `includeDirs`. Follow-ups reuse the returned structured Thread ID and omit `includeDirs`, because `codex exec resume` does not support `--add-dir`; a resumed call that still passes `includeDirs` is rejected by every Codex transport (split `ask-codex`, unified `ask-llm`) rather than silently dropping the directories. Feedback is relayed and source-verified before Cursor edits. Interrupts cancel the MCP call; unavailable tools/models, incomplete unified schemas, partial failures, and any Codex quota fallback are reported rather than hidden.

Example:

```text
/codex-pair model=gpt-6.2-sol effort=high include=packages/api,packages/shared review this migration
```

With the plugin loaded, the unified `ask-llm` tool is the bundled transport: `/codex-pair` uses it with `provider: "codex"` and every option pinned; unsupported combinations (including `includeDirs` on a resumed thread) are rejected instead of stripped. A separately user-installed `ask-codex` leaf is preferred when exposed. If neither transport is present, run `ask-llm setup --host cursor`, follow any printed guidance, authenticate Codex, and reload from **Cursor Settings → Tools & MCP** or restart Cursor Agent. Earlier registrations are covered by [Migration](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/reference/migration).

## `/grok-pair` route safety

When Cursor itself is the host, `/grok-pair` does not recursively invoke Cursor Agent. Select `xai-api` or `grok-cli` through the bundled unified `ask-llm` with provider, harness, exact model, and effort all pinned, or through a separately user-installed `ask-grok` leaf when exposed; there is no fallback. Claude Code may instead select Grok through the model-neutral `ask-cursor-agent` tool; that route keeps host, provider, Cursor harness, exact catalog ID, and optional display label separate and refuses Auto or cross-provider substitution.

If neither direct transport is exposed, run `ask-llm setup --host cursor` and reload Cursor. The `xai-api` route needs `XAI_API_KEY` in the MCP process environment; keep literal secrets in user-level configuration and never commit them. The `grok-cli` route needs authenticated Grok Build with headless JSON flags visible in `grok --help`. Reload from **Cursor Settings → Tools & MCP** or restart Cursor Agent, then invoke `/grok-pair` again. Unified startup probes both direct harnesses, so a CLI-only login works without setting `ASK_GROK_HARNESS=grok-cli`; the request still pins `harness: "grok-cli"`, and no API fallback occurs. A CLI-only call that omits `harness` fails with a diagnostic naming that pin (or `ASK_GROK_HARNESS=grok-cli`), and an explicit `ASK_GROK_HARNESS` makes startup readiness track that harness alone.

## Lifecycle differences

| Capability | Claude Code | Cursor Agent |
|---|---|---|
| `/codex-pair` | Marker-gated continuous hooks plus dashboard | On-demand skill-backed persisted reviewer session |
| Registration | Claude plugin + `.mcp.json` (Codex only) | Cursor Plugin Agent Skills + `mcp.json` (unified `ask-llm` only, started with `node` from the plugin's own pinned `@ask-llm/mcp` release; split servers user-installed) |
| Include directories | Per-edit context from marker/project | Explicit safe relative `includeDirs` on first Codex call |
| Completion gate | Optional Claude Stop hook | Explicit completed/cancelled/failed session report |
| Cancellation | Claude hook/provider process lifecycle | Cursor MCP AbortSignal/interrupt |
| Pause / resume / ack | `/codex-pair-pause`, `/codex-pair-resume`, `/codex-pair-ack` toggle the background hook | Setup installs the portable skills, but they do not control Cursor's on-demand session; end or restart that session instead |

The portable contract is canonical in `packages/llm-mcp/skills/ask-llm-codex-pair/pairing-contract.md`; host adapters must not claim lifecycle guarantees their host does not provide.

### Pi host notes

Source: https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/compatibility/pi.html

Pi owns your conversation, host model, tools and lifecycle. Ask LLM supplies native tools backed by the same provider executors and schemas as other hosts; Pi does not need MCP configuration. Your Pi account and reviewer accounts have separate authentication and billing.

## Prerequisites

- Node.js 24+
- Pi 0.83.0 or newer
- one or more provider runtimes:
  - authenticated `codex` CLI for Codex reviews, images, verification, and default pairing
  - authenticated `claude` CLI for explicitly selected Claude pairing
  - authenticated enterprise `gemini` CLI for Gemini
  - local Ollama server with the requested model pulled
  - authenticated [supported `agy` version](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/providers/antigravity#prerequisites) for Antigravity

The published Pi support floor always matches the oldest exact host version exercised by the `pi-package-smoke` CI matrix; currently both the 0.83.0 floor and current 0.84.2 host are tested in isolated environments.

The extension reads provider credentials only indirectly by invoking the provider package/CLI. It never copies keys or Pi credentials.

## Connection

Follow [Install](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/start/install), then restart Pi or use `/reload`. Setup registers the globally installed extension as a local package and fills the shared skills folder. The extension prints a notice naming `ask-llm setup --host pi` if no portable workflow is found. Earlier npm installations are left unchanged with [migration guidance](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/reference/migration).

## Skills and tools

Invoke a skill explicitly with `/skill:<name>` or describe the workflow naturally. Pi progressively loads the same canonical `SKILL.md` files used by Claude Code, then follows their Pi adapter.

Representative commands:

```text
/skill:ask-llm-review
/skill:ask-llm-multi-review
/skill:ask-llm-compare gemini,codex explain this API design
/skill:ask-llm-brainstorm antigravity,codex review this architecture
/skill:ask-llm-brainstorm grok@cursor-agent:grok-4.7-high,codex@cursor-agent:gpt-6.2-sol-high review this architecture
/skill:ask-llm-codex-image create a monochrome architecture diagram
/skill:ask-llm-codex-verify
/skill:ask-llm-codex-pair
```

The Cursor `gpt-6.2-sol-high` example follows the `<codex-slug>-high` naming but is unverified; confirm the exact ID with `agent --list-models` before use.

Pi reads these skills from the shared skills folder that `ask-llm setup --host pi` fills; the package itself ships only the extension. `ask-llm-fable-review` is not installed: independent Fable review would require a nested Pi session or provider bridge. `ask-llm-grok-pair` is installed for other hosts and refuses on Pi, because Grok pairing still needs a dedicated Pi consent/lifecycle adapter.

For `/skill:ask-llm-codex-pair`, check the [portable writer applicability rule](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/advanced/codex-pair) first. The native `/codex-pair` commands described below use their separate consent flow.

Native tools (Pi has no MCP client, so the extension registers them with the MCP server's input schemas; see the [host parity matrix](https://github.com/Lykhoyda/ask-llm/blob/main/docs/HOST-PARITY.md)):

| Tool | Contract |
|---|---|
| `ask-llm` | the MCP `ask-llm` schema (`provider`, `model`, `reasoningEffort`, `includeDirs`, `sessionId`, `harness`, `preferred`, `noFallback`, `sandbox`) and the same `AskResponse` in `details.structuredContent`; `provider` uses the same detected availability and exclusions as MCP |
| `multi-llm` | the MCP `multi-llm` schema and report; omitted `providers` means every detected provider |
| `ask-cursor-agent` | the MCP schema: model-neutral Cursor harness with separate provider + exact account model ID, safe relative `includeDirs`, and optional returned/resumed Cursor `sessionId`; the exact ID is echoed as `model`, Cursor's label stays separate as `reportedModel`, and read-only ask mode never falls back |

For `provider: "antigravity"`, use `reasoningEffort` with a compatible base model and `noFallback: true` for a single attempt. See [Antigravity](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/providers/antigravity#tools) for supported tiers and the required execution opt-in.

Deprecated aliases, kept for existing skills and prompts:

| Tool | Contract |
|---|---|
| `ask-codex` | complete prompt/model/reasoning/session/includeDirs/preferred/noFallback/sandbox schema; read-only default |
| `ask-gemini` | prompt/model/session schema and canonical quota fallback |
| `ask-grok` | prompt/model/reasoning plus explicit `xai-api` or `grok-cli` harness; no model/harness fallback |
| `ask-ollama` | prompt/model/session schema; local-only, no silent model substitution |
| `ask-antigravity` | prompt/includeDirs schema and supported-`agy` checks |
| `ask-multi` | same prompt to 2–5 unique providers via bounded `Promise.allSettled`, with per-provider options; stable input-order records and explicit failures |

Displayed tool text is bounded to Pi's 50KB/2000-line policy; structured payloads remain complete. Provider failures throw, so Pi records `isError: true`; Ask LLM usage remains raw metadata in `details` and is not misreported as Pi host-model cost.

## Pi codex-pair consent

Create `.codex-pair/context.md` in a trusted Pi project. Choose the reviewer in the initial fenced frontmatter and put project invariants below the fence. Keep `.codex-pair/` out of version control.

For a Codex review of edits from an independent writer:

```markdown
---
reviewer: codex
reasoningEffort: high
---
Amounts use integer cents. Retrying a payment must preserve its idempotency key.
```

If your Pi writer is OpenAI or OpenAI Codex, explicitly choose Claude:

```markdown
---
reviewer: claude
timeoutMs: 600000
---
Amounts use integer cents. Retrying a payment must preserve its idempotency key.
```

In interactive Pi, run `/codex-pair` to approve the selected CLI. The prompt names the CLI, model, any Codex quota fallback, and the amount of edited-file content and marker body the review can receive. It states that the CLI uses its locally configured account; it does not display an account identifier. Check that CLI's login before granting consent. Codex and Claude can use different accounts. Each review uses the selected account's quota or billing. Project trust and an affirmative grant for the canonical project root and selected reviewer are both required. Claude Code's template and catch-up commands provide no Pi grant.

Use `/codex-pair status` to check the selected reviewer and its authorization. A grant for a different reviewer requires a new confirmation and replaces the previous grant. Declining leaves the previous grant in place and sends nothing. Use `/codex-pair revoke` to remove the grant, including when the marker frontmatter is malformed.

The user-owned allowlist is at `$PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR/ask-llm/codex-pair-projects.json` (usually `~/.pi/agent/ask-llm/codex-pair-projects.json`). Existing version 1 grants authorize Codex only. A grant or revoke migrates valid entries to version 2 and keeps other projects' timestamps. A legacy build reads the version 2 file as unauthorized. Run one build against the allowlist at a time. If you roll back, use a fresh legacy allowlist and explicitly reauthorize Codex through the older Pi command. Claude grants do not carry back. A previously reviewed file can receive one cold review on its next eligible edit.

### Writer identity and review settings

Pi uses the model that wrote the edit and separately checks its current model selection before dispatch and delivery. `openai` and `openai-codex` are Codex-family writers, `anthropic` is Claude-family, and `xai` is Grok-family. A reviewer refuses a writer from its own family. A custom or router provider whose family Pi cannot establish is treated as unknown. Matching reviewer consent still applies, and the finding includes the reported provider/model when available. The [portable skill writer rule](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/advanced/codex-pair) applies when invoking the skill.

Plain markers use the defaults. A setting below the initial fence is project context. Pi refuses invalid reviewer values and unclosed initial frontmatter. The precedence for valid settings is:

| Setting | Pi resolution |
|---|---|
| `reviewer` | `codex` by default, or explicit `claude` |
| Codex `model` | Marker, `ASK_CODEX_MODEL`, then `gpt-6.2-sol` |
| Codex `reasoningEffort` | Marker, `ASK_CODEX_REASONING_EFFORT`, then `high`. Accepted values are `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`, and `ultra`. CLI and model support determines which values work. |
| Codex `fallbackModel` | Marker, `ASK_CODEX_FALLBACK_MODEL`, then `gpt-6.1-terra`. A primary quota failure can make one attempt at a distinct configured fallback on the same CLI and account. |
| Claude model and effort | The Claude CLI always selects `claude-opus-5-5`. Effort is unknown and there is no fallback. Codex pins and `ASK_CLAUDE_MODEL` do not influence this route. |
| `timeoutMs` | Per attempt, marker then `ASK_CODEX_TIMEOUT_MS` or `ASK_CLAUDE_TIMEOUT_MS`. Codex also uses legacy `GMCPT_TIMEOUT_MS` before its 800000 ms default. Claude defaults to 600000 ms. |
| `debounceMs` and `debounceMaxMs` | Marker, `ASK_CODEX_DEBOUNCE_MS` and `ASK_CODEX_DEBOUNCE_MAX_MS`, then 15000 and 60000 ms. A zero settle delay is valid. The cap must be positive. |
| `maxFileBytes` | Positive UTF-8 byte cap from the marker, `CODEX_PAIR_MAX_FILE_BYTES`, then 20000 bytes. Oversized file or marker content gets a partial view. |
| `surfaceThreshold` | Marker value `high`, `med` (default), or `low`. |

Numeric settings must be integers no larger than 2147483647; invalid values fall through to the next setting. Timeouts, model errors and unrecognized reviews produce a failure without a cross-provider retry. Each reviewer runs from the canonical project root. Codex runs read-only. Claude uses safe mode and read-only tools. If Claude refuses to start inside a Claude Code session, launch Pi separately.

### Findings and lifecycle

Pi observes successful built-in `edit` and `write` events, coalesces each edit burst and reviews settled file content. It persists findings, then delivers them as advisory messages without starting another model turn. The header identifies the selected reviewer and attempt model, any Claude model reported by the CLI, and the writer. Pi treats all findings as advisory, including when a marker sets `blockOn: HIGH`. Pi log entries do not count toward Claude Code's Stop gate or catch-up coverage.

```text
/codex-pair                 # check or grant consent
/codex-pair status
/codex-pair revoke
/codex-pair-pause
/codex-pair-resume
/codex-pair-ack <hash> <reason>
```

Pause, revoke and incompatible model changes suppress work already in progress. Shutdown, reload, new session, resume and fork close the old session, cancel its active reviewer and release its locks. Compatible pending findings can replay after restart. Claims prevent concurrent delivery, and each replay preserves `details.findingId` so receivers can deduplicate a crash after delivery and before cleanup. Logs, cache, pause state, acknowledgements and consent survive shutdown.

Pairing works in TUI, RPC and long-lived JSON modes. Grant consent in TUI. One-shot print mode skips pairing.

## Host feature matrix

See the [host parity matrix](https://github.com/Lykhoyda/ask-llm/blob/main/docs/HOST-PARITY.md) for tools, skills, options, diagnostics, pairing, subagents, and the Stop gate across all supported hosts. The following workflow-specific limits supplement that matrix:

| Capability | Claude Code | Cursor Agent | Codex CLI host | Pi |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Independent `fable-review` | Yes | No; excluded | No | No; excluded |
| `codex-image` | Yes | provider-dependent | provider-dependent | Yes, explicit workspace-write opt-in |
| Grok pairing | Explicit Cursor/xAI/CLI routes | Direct xAI/CLI routes | Direct xAI/CLI routes | Skill is installed but refuses; no consent/lifecycle adapter |
| Pairing in one-shot print mode | Hook-dependent | On-demand skill | On-demand skill | **No** |

## Update and remove

Follow [Upgrade and remove](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/start/upgrade-remove) for Pi package removal, workflow cleanup and retained user state, and [Migration](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/reference/migration) for earlier npm installations.

## Troubleshooting

- **Package absent:** run `pi list`; rerun the [Install](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/start/install) setup step.
- **Skills absent:** confirm `enableSkillCommands` is true, run `/reload`, and check `/skill:ask-llm-review`; if it is missing, run `ask-llm setup --host pi`. `ask-llm-fable-review` should remain absent.
- **Project package absent:** trust the project (`/trust`, then restart) or use `--approve` for a one-run check.
- **Pairing refuses a marker:** project trust and user-owned consent are both required; run `/codex-pair` in interactive Pi.
- **Provider unavailable:** run the named CLI directly once to install/authenticate it (`codex`, `gemini`, `agy`) or start Ollama and pull the configured model. The native tool returns the provider package's actionable error.
- **Pairing seems silent:** use TUI/RPC/long-lived JSON, check pause status with `/codex-pair`, and inspect `.codex-pair/log.jsonl`. Print mode is intentionally unsupported.
- **Need a refresh after update:** run `/reload` or restart Pi.


## Providers

- [Codex](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/providers/codex.html)
- [Claude](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/providers/claude.html)
- [Grok](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/providers/grok.html)
- [Antigravity](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/providers/antigravity.html)
- [Ollama](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/providers/ollama.html)
- [Gemini](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/providers/gemini.html)

## Operation

### Diagnostics / doctor

Source: https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/operation/diagnostics.html

Run diagnostics before changing configuration:

```bash
ask-llm doctor
ask-llm doctor --json
```

The report distinguishes these states:

| State | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Installed | The provider runtime or host is present |
| Registered | The host has a registration; this alone does not prove tool availability |
| Authenticated | Authentication evidence is available; unknown means it was not established |
| Permitted | The provider's execution gate allows a call |
| Exercised | A live provider call succeeded |

Ordinary diagnostics do not make paid inference calls. The host report includes restart instructions, manual guidance and the host's [compatibility matrix](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/compatibility/hosts) rows. A leftover config directory is a clue, not proof that a host is installed.

Google route checks run only for an installed Gemini or Antigravity CLI and use environment variable names only. Doctor warns about possible alternate billing when Gemini sees `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `GOOGLE_API_KEY`, `GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI` or `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`, or when Antigravity sees `AGY_ADC_AUTH` or `GEMINI_API_KEY`. With only `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` or `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT_ID`, or with no signals, the route check is skipped and the seat and funding remain unverified. Cached Cloud credentials and pay-as-you-go settings may still affect billing. Doctor leaves Gemini CLI registration unchecked because its settings file also holds authentication preferences. See [Google authentication](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/operation/authentication) for the consumer-plan terms boundary.

## Optional live check

`ask-llm doctor --live` skips Gemini and Antigravity model exercises because their routes and funding are unverified. It exercises other ready, permitted providers with a small prompt in a temporary directory. That prompt may consume quota or incur provider charges.

Live doctor also reports [Antigravity quota metadata](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/providers/antigravity#quota-diagnostics) on supported versions. Default doctor starts zero agy processes.

## Formats

```bash
ask-llm doctor --format toon
ask-llm doctor --format toon --full
```

JSON remains the full automation interface; TOON is a bounded, versioned, provider-only presentation and cannot be combined with `--live`. Doctor exits 1 on an error, 0 on an OK or warning report, and 2 on invalid arguments. The existing server's `doctor` mode is provider-only; `ask-llm doctor` adds hosts in text and JSON formats.

Use `ask-llm doctor --help` for the exact options. If the report is healthy but a call fails, inspect [authentication](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/operation/authentication), the provider's limits, and [troubleshooting](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/resources/troubleshooting).

### Authentication

Source: https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/operation/authentication.html

Ask LLM connects your host to the provider accounts you already use. Installing and signing in to a provider is your responsibility; setup never performs provider login.

| Provider or route | What must be ready |
|---|---|
| [Codex](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/providers/codex) | Installed Codex CLI, authenticated account |
| [Claude](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/providers/claude) | Installed Claude Code CLI, authenticated account; a host other than Claude Code |
| [Grok](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/providers/grok) | Authenticated official Grok Build with headless JSON support, or an explicitly configured metered xAI API key |
| Cursor Agent | Authenticated Cursor CLI and exact model ID from `agent --list-models` |
| [Antigravity](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/providers/antigravity) | Authenticated [supported agy version](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/providers/antigravity#prerequisites) and explicit execution opt-in; opt-in has no read-only guarantee |
| [Ollama](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/providers/ollama) | Running local server and the requested model pulled |
| [Gemini](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/providers/gemini) | Authenticated CLI and an eligible Standard/Enterprise seat |

For subscription-backed routes, no separate model API key is needed. Grok's `xai-api` route requires `XAI_API_KEY` in the host's server environment and incurs metered charges. Pin `grok-cli` to use Grok Build rather than the default API route; routes never fail over to one another.

Provider credentials stay in the provider's login/configuration flow. The xAI API route reads the key from the process environment to authenticate requests; Ask LLM does not log or return it. Keep keys out of committed configuration.

Run `ask-llm doctor` to see what is installed and which providers have local authentication evidence. Gemini and Antigravity report authentication as unknown. Doctor looks only for Google route signal names in its environment and leaves credentials and mixed Google settings unread. Signs of API keys, Vertex AI, ADC, cached Cloud credentials, or pay-as-you-go settings can indicate possible alternate billing. A project variable alone leaves the Gemini seat and account funding unproven. Confirm the intended account and seat or subscription in the provider's own settings. Google's consumer-plan support excludes third-party headless Antigravity wrappers. See the [Antigravity terms guidance](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/providers/antigravity).

Restart the host after adding a provider or changing its environment. See [diagnostics](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/operation/diagnostics) for the optional quota-consuming live check.

### Data flow

Source: https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/operation/data-flow.html

The coding assistant gathers the diff, selected files and relevant project context, then sends that material to the provider you choose. That provider returns an opinion; your assistant remains the editor. Hosting Ask LLM in Claude Code does not mean Claude is the reviewer, and Claude Code cannot consult a nested Claude session.

## Review boundaries

Codex, Claude, Gemini, Grok and Cursor review routes use read-only controls. Antigravity refuses execution by default; enabling it does not give a read-only guarantee. Local Ollama inference stays on the configured server; use a local endpoint when your material must stay on your machine. A remote `OLLAMA_HOST` sends material to that endpoint.

Ask LLM sends no telemetry. Selected hosted providers receive your prompts and code under their own policies, and the host can retain its conversation. Grok's API route uses `store:false`; that request setting is not a guarantee about every provider retention policy.

## Request Flow




For a single-provider call (`ask-llm` with `provider: "gemini"`), only one of the provider lanes fires. For `multi-llm`, both fire in parallel via `Promise.all` inside the Ask LLM process; per-provider failures are isolated, so one provider hitting quota doesn't fail the whole call.

## Connection details

Provider executors apply their own controls:

- **Quota fallback**: Gemini Pro → Flash on `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`; Codex `gpt-6.2-sol` → `gpt-6.1-terra` on quota errors
- **Stdin handling**: Codex needs an EOF-terminated pipe rather than `/dev/null`, otherwise it errors out
- **PATH resolution**: macOS GUI clients (Claude Desktop) don't inherit your shell's PATH; the server resolves it from your login shell at startup
- **Live progressive output**: Gemini's `--output-format stream-json` deltas are parsed and forwarded to MCP progress notifications, so users see Gemini's prose unfolding rather than a frozen wait
- **Session continuity**: see [Tools and schemas](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/reference/tools#sessions) for provider support and first-turn requirements
- **Read-only Claude consultations**: Claude consultations use safe mode and exposes only Read, Glob, and Grep; the MCP host performs any edits
- **Structured responses**: every `ask-*` tool returns both human-readable text AND a structured `AskResponse` (provider, response, model, sessionId, usage) via MCP `outputSchema` so programmatic clients don't have to parse the response footer

You don't need to think about any of this; it's just the infrastructure that makes the natural-language flow work reliably.

## Session storage

See [Tools and schemas](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/reference/tools#sessions) for provider session storage and retention, and the [Cursor Agent tool](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/reference/tools) for its separate conversation IDs.

Usage totals are in memory and reset when the server restarts. Pairing writes user-owned logs and state under `.codex-pair/`; see [pair review](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/advanced/codex-pair). Do not treat model agreement as evidence that a claim is correct. Validate it against source, tests and requirements.

### Costs and Fallbacks

Source: https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/operation/costs.html

Hosted CLI providers (Gemini, Codex, Claude, Antigravity) auto-select a sensible default model with automatic fallback on provider-specific conditions — quota/rate-limit exhaustion, and for Antigravity also a rejected shipped model slug (see the table below). Grok and Ollama never substitute another model: Grok sends the selected API or Grok CLI catalog ID unchanged, while Ollama uses exactly the model you pull. **Most users should never override the model parameter**; the defaults are tuned for quality.

## Defaults & Fallbacks




| Provider | Default | Fallback | Trigger |
|---|---|---|---|
| Gemini | `gemini-4-argon` | `gemini-3.8-flash` | `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` quota error or "exhausted your capacity" pattern |
| Codex | `gpt-6.2-sol` | `gpt-6.1-terra` | Quota errors (`rate_limit_exceeded`, `429`, `insufficient_quota`) |
| Claude | `opus` (Opus 5.5, `claude-opus-5-5`) | `sonnet` | Claude Code native fallback when Opus is overloaded or unavailable |
| Grok | `grok-4.7` (`reasoning.effort=high`) | none | Every error is terminal; requested ID is sent unchanged |
| Antigravity | Submits `gemini-4-neon` with `--effort high` | Submits `gemini-4-hydrogen` on a rate limit. Retries once without `--model` if agy rejects a shipped slug. Both retain the effective effort (`high` or the `ASK_ANTIGRAVITY_EFFORT` override). | Rate limit or model-unavailable error for a shipped slug |
| Ollama | `qwen3.8:27b` | none | Local, no fallback; a missing model returns a clear `ollama pull` error |

Structured output includes a model label and `usage.fellBack`. For Antigravity, the label is the slug submitted for the successful attempt, including `gemini-4-hydrogen` after a successful rate-limit fallback, or `agy default` after a successful model-less recovery. The backend model is unverified in each case. Grok and Ollama never fall back, so their `fellBack` values are always `false`.

`codex-pair` defaults to `gpt-6.2-sol` at `high` reasoning effort and quota-falls back to `gpt-6.1-terra`. Unpinned Codex consultations also use `gpt-6.2-sol`.

Codex uses `medium` reasoning effort for ordinary calls to preserve the previous default behavior. The quality-first `/ask-llm-review` and `/ask-llm-brainstorm` skills use `high`. Direct `ask-llm` with `provider: "codex"` calls can override this with `reasoningEffort` (`low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`, or `ultra`). `ultra` is opt-in only: Codex's catalog describes it as maximum reasoning with automatic task delegation, so review and brainstorm defaults stay at `high`.

## Account costs

Review calls consume the quota or billing of the provider account you authenticate. Ask LLM does not enable billing, buy credits, or alter spending limits. Grok's metered xAI API is an explicit option requiring `XAI_API_KEY`; Grok Build and Cursor routes follow their own plans. Ollama uses local compute. Model agreement does not prove correctness.

## Choosing a Provider

Different providers excel at different things. Pick by what you're doing, not by which is "best":

| Task | Suggested provider | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Targeted code reasoning, refactor critique | **Codex** | GPT-6.2 Sol is the default; see [Codex Pair](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/advanced/codex-pair#configuration-knobs) for pair-review defaults |
| Claude second opinion while working in Codex | **Claude** | Opus 5.5 (`opus`) review through Claude Code CLI, with native session continuation and read-only file access |
| Grok 4.7 independent critique | **Grok** | Exact model selection, configurable reasoning depth, structured JSON Schema output |
| Private / air-gapped analysis | **Ollama** | Runs locally, nothing leaves your machine |
| Antigravity second opinion | **Antigravity** | Unified `ask-llm` with `provider: "antigravity"` and local opt-in. See [Google's consumer-plan terms and account checks](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/providers/antigravity). |
| Gemini CLI review | **Gemini** | An [existing, eligible Gemini Code Assist Standard or Enterprise seat](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/providers/gemini). Access to the pinned models is unverified. |
| "What do they all think?" comparison | **Multi-LLM** (`multi-llm` tool or `/ask-llm-compare` skill) | Parallel dispatch, see all responses side-by-side |
| Code review with verified findings | **`/ask-llm-multi-review` skill** | Antigravity + Codex in parallel, then verifies each finding against source |

## Overriding the Model

For a Gemini CLI model override, see [Flash-Lite configuration and seat eligibility](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/providers/gemini#flash-lite).

Pass `model` explicitly when you have a reason to:

```text
Use ask-llm with provider gemini and model gemini-3.8-flash to quickly check this CSS file
```

Or programmatically:

```json
{ "name": "ask-llm", "arguments": { "provider": "gemini", "model": "gemini-3.8-flash", "prompt": "..." } }
```

For Grok, choose the harness first. Discover API IDs with authenticated `GET https://api.x.ai/v1/models`, or CLI IDs with `grok models`, then pass the desired ID unchanged. Reasoning depth is a separate `reasoningEffort` parameter (`low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`), not a model suffix. There is no harness or model fallback. Cursor Agent is separate and model-neutral: `ask-cursor-agent` requires a canonical provider family (`claude`, `codex`, `gemini`, `grok`) plus an exact account ID from `agent --list-models` (for example a Cursor Grok ID may differ from xAI's API ID); the ID must belong to that family, and Cursor Auto or other noncanonical IDs are refused.

For Codex, common overrides:

```text
Use ask-llm with provider codex and model gpt-6.1-terra to summarize this commit
```

For Ollama, you can request any model you've pulled:

```bash
ollama pull deepseek-coder:6.7b
```

```text
Use ask-llm with provider ollama and model deepseek-coder:6.7b to review this implementation
```

Use the unified `ask-llm` tool with `provider: "antigravity"`. For model and effort overrides, see the [Antigravity configuration reference](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/providers/antigravity#config).

## Token Limits & Cost

| Provider | Context window | Cost model |
|---|---|---|
| Gemini CLI | Depends on available model | Existing, eligible Gemini Code Assist Standard or Enterprise seat |
| Codex GPT-6.2 Astra / GPT-6.2 Sol | Per OpenAI's published context window | Your authenticated account’s quota/billing |
| Grok 4.7 | 500k tokens on xAI API | API is metered; Grok CLI follows its authenticated plan |
| Cursor Agent harness | Per selected catalog model | Included usage/on-demand spend follows the user's Cursor plan; Ask LLM never changes spend settings |
| Codex GPT-6.1 Terra | Per OpenAI's published context window | Cheaper, faster fallback target |
| Ollama | Per model (e.g., 256k for qwen3.8) | Local compute and hardware |

## Track What You're Spending

Token usage is exposed live via:

- **Per-call**: `result.structuredContent.usage` on `ask-*` tool responses (provider, model, inputTokens, outputTokens, cachedTokens, thinkingTokens, durationMs, fellBack). See [Antigravity tools](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/providers/antigravity#tools) for agy's usage reporting.
- **Per-session aggregate**: call the `get-usage-stats` MCP tool, or read the `usage://current-session` MCP Resource for a JSON snapshot
- **In the REPL**: type `/usage` for a markdown-formatted breakdown

This is in-memory only; no persistence to disk, resets when the MCP server restarts.

## Recommendations by Use Case

- **General code review** → defaults are correct; let the fallback chain handle quota
- **Whole-codebase analysis with Google** → use the [Gemini CLI route](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/providers/gemini) if you have an eligible seat, or review the [Antigravity route prerequisites](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/providers/antigravity#prerequisites).
- **Quick fixes, fast iteration** → request Flash or `gpt-6.1-terra` explicitly to skip the flagship→fallback round-trip
- **Grok consultation** → `ask-grok`; confirm xAI pricing and data transfer first, then use exact model IDs with no fallback
- **Privacy-sensitive code** → `ask-ollama`, never leaves your machine
- **Multi-perspective debate** → `multi-llm` or `/ask-llm-brainstorm` skill; Claude weighs verified vs inferred


## Advanced

### Codex Pair

Source: https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/advanced/codex-pair.html

In the portable `/codex-pair` skill, a positively identified Codex writer with a Codex reviewer ends before setup or consent in one message: the same family reviewing itself is not an independent review; use `/grok-pair`; `completed (not applicable)`. It asks no question and makes no review call. This depends on the writer's model family, never the host name: Cursor and Pi can run other families. An unknown writer or a different provider keeps the existing adapter behavior. Pi's native `/codex-pair` command also supports explicit Claude review of Codex-family edits after reviewer consent.

Codex-pair supports each host with a different lifecycle adapter. The detailed detached-worker and Stop-gate material on this page describes **Claude Code**. On **Cursor Agent** there is no background reviewer: `/codex-pair` runs an on-demand, consent-gated persisted Codex session (through a user-installed `ask-codex` leaf when exposed, otherwise the fully pinned unified `ask-llm`) and the `-ack`/`-pause`/`-resume` toggles are not exposed; see [Cursor Agent Host](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/compatibility/cursor). On **Pi**, successful `tool_result` edit/write events feed an in-process debounce; findings are delivered with non-triggering `steer`; the marker, project trust and consent for the selected reviewer and canonical project are required; shutdown aborts active review work; blocking Stop-gate and one-shot print parity are unsupported. See [Pi Host Support](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/compatibility/pi#pi-codex-pair-consent).

**codex-pair** is the plugin's flagship feature: continuous, opt-in code review where Codex reads every file Claude edits. It is the recall-first complement to the on-demand `/codex-review` skill. Setup never enables pairing. The hook is always loaded but **self-gates on a project marker file** and stays completely silent (zero cost, zero Codex calls) until a project opts in. Once enabled, a burst of edits to one file coalesces into a single debounced review of the **settled** file state, run by a detached worker; verdicts surface to Claude on both hook channels (transcript `systemMessage` plus model-visible `additionalContext`) and drain on the next edit, the next user prompt, or at turn end via the Stop hook.

> **Why this exists**: in a four-task benchmark recorded in the project's [decision log](https://github.com/Lykhoyda/ask-llm/blob/main/docs/DECISIONS.md) (four structurally different task types: CRUD endpoint, URL shortener, RFC-spec implementation, stateful business logic, chosen so the result would generalize across domains) Claude alone caught **2 of 10** probes; Claude + `/codex-review` caught **7 of 10**; Claude + `codex-pair` caught **10 of 10**. The three probes `/codex-review` missed exemplified the **"looks fine, runs wrong"** class: code that compiles, lints, and type-checks but produces wrong results because of an implicit invariant the model couldn't infer from a single file. codex-pair's recall-first HIGH/MED/LOW grading catches that class. **The improvement is task-agnostic**, reproduced across all four tasks, not just the headline one. The two surfaces are **complementary, not competing**. (A subsequent lived-experience audit confirms the benchmark holds in real flow on this very repo.)

## Grok CLI

```text
Grok file edit / shell call -> shared pair hook -> Codex Sol (default)
                                             └-> Claude Opus 5.5 (opt-in)
                                                      |
                                       additionalContext -> next Grok step
```

Grok CLI 1.0.70 supports the same marker, review prompt, findings format, cache, log and pause/resume/ack state. Reviews run synchronously so the note reaches the model before the hook exits; Grok ignores the guide's `async` field. Catch-up is unavailable on Grok: it has neither a Stop gate nor a prompt drain. Existing Claude Code behavior and defaults remain unchanged.

Create `.codex-pair/context.md` with project invariants and optional frontmatter:

```markdown
---
reviewer: codex
---
Project invariants for the reviewer.
```

`reviewer: codex` is the default (`gpt-6.2-sol`, high effort, existing disclosed Terra quota fallback). `reviewer: claude` opts into pinned `claude-opus-5-5`, read tools only, no model/provider fallback. Marker `reviewer` is the sole reviewer setting. Invalid settings refuse; choosing a reviewer from the writer's own family also refuses (for example Claude reviewing Claude Code).
