The Claude timeout is marker `timeoutMs`, then `ASK_CLAUDE_TIMEOUT_MS`, then 600 seconds. Existing Codex settings still apply to Codex.

Register this yourself in `~/.grok/hooks/ask-llm-pair.json` (or `$GROK_HOME/hooks/ask-llm-pair.json`), using the absolute installed `@ask-llm/mcp` directory as `<package-root>`. Keep a single pair hook registration and remove any duplicate imported Claude pair hook for Grok:

```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PostToolUse": [{
      "matcher": "search_replace|run_terminal_command",
      "hooks": [{
        "type": "command",
        "command": "node \"<package-root>/scripts/grok-pair-watch.mjs\"",
        "timeout": 1800
      }]
    }]
  }
}
```

Restart Grok and inspect `/hooks`. Global hooks run under headless `grok -p`; project `.grok/hooks/` files need folder trust, which also trusts the folder's other integrations. `ask-llm setup` does not install this hook or change trust files. Tests use isolated `HOME` and `GROK_HOME` only.

File edits review the resulting file. **Shell reviews cover the command text as given, with no diff or resulting file contents**; all shell calls are eligible because commands cannot reliably be classified as writes. The prompt explains this coverage limit. Shell logs and include/ignore filters use a synthetic `[shell command]` path under the event cwd. Oversized commands receive a partial view. Findings are advisory after the edit has already happened.

Use the portable pause, resume and ack skills against the same `.codex-pair/` state. Grok honors the existing file-scoped acknowledgement hash in advisory output; original findings remain in the log. See the [Grok skill adapter](https://github.com/Lykhoyda/ask-llm/blob/main/packages/llm-mcp/skills/ask-llm-codex-pair/grok.md) for setup, acknowledgement hashes and status reporting. Pairing sends file/command context through the selected authenticated reviewer CLI and consumes that account's quota; this adapter never calls the metered xAI API. Cursor Agent per-edit integration and Codex CLI per-edit hooks remain outside this adapter.

The remaining sections describe the Claude Code lifecycle unless another host is named.

## Setup

Run the `/codex-pair` slash command in the project where you want continuous review. On first run (no marker present) on Claude Code it copies a committed `.codex-pair.example/context.md` from the repository root to `.codex-pair/context.md` at that root without asking; it never overwrites an existing marker. Without a template it offers interactive setup with auto-detected project context and writes `.codex-pair/context.md` in the current directory after confirmation. Setup finds existing markers by walking up from the current directory through the repository root. Either way it keeps `.codex-pair/` out of git through the local exclude file described below. You can also create the marker by hand:

```bash
mkdir -p .codex-pair
cat > .codex-pair/context.md <<'EOF'
---
blockOn: false
---
# .codex-pair/context.md

This is a payment-processing service. All currency calculations must
use integer cents internally (floating-point loses precision on every
charge). Concurrent requests are real. URL inputs are untrusted.

[Add domain invariants Codex can't infer from one file. Examples:
 Security: "all routes check user.role".
 Specs: "protocol XYZ must be followed".
 State: "cart syncs to localStorage on every mutation".
 Concurrency: "this handler must be idempotent under retry".]
EOF
```

On Claude Code, the marker file opts the project into review; `CODEX_PAIR_DISABLED=1` or a pause sentinel still prevents reviews. Its content is review context. Interactively drafted markers explicitly set `blockOn: false` for advisory review; template copies preserve their settings, including `blockOn`. An existing marker without `blockOn` remains advisory. On Pi, marker presence is only the repository-side gate: it never authorizes provider transfer/cost without Pi project trust and separate interactive `/codex-pair` consent stored outside the repository.

**Do NOT commit the `.codex-pair/` directory**: keep it ignored. Each contributor's review context is their own; one developer iterating on prompt wording shouldn't dirty the shared history. The hook itself is project-policy (it's in the plugin); the marker is per-developer opt-in. Every state artifact (marker, log, cache, `ignore` globs, pause sentinel, inflight locks) nests under the single directory; one ignore line covers everything:

```gitignore
.codex-pair/
```

`/codex-pair` setup on Claude Code appends that line to git's local exclude file, the path `git rev-parse --git-path info/exclude` prints. A linked worktree has a `.git` file rather than a folder, so the path comes from git; all worktrees of a repository share that file. Setup never edits `.gitignore` and skips the exclude entry when git already ignores the entire `.codex-pair/` directory. It verifies directory-wide exclusion after appending and exits non-zero if higher-priority rules still prevent it. Add the line to `.gitignore` or your global ignore file yourself if you prefer.

For a new contributor or a fresh worktree, commit a template at `.codex-pair.example/context.md` in the repository root: `/codex-pair` copies it with no questions, and each developer can then edit their own copy. You can run the same step directly from the project with `node packages/llm-mcp/scripts/codex-pair-log.mjs setup`. Its first word reports the outcome: `created`, `exists`, `no-template`, `not-git`, `invalid-template`, `invalid-marker` or `ignore-failed`. Templates and markers must be regular files inside the repository with no symlinked path components; invalid paths are refused before copying or changing ignore rules. Setup verifies directory-wide exclusion before copying a template; exclusion failure leaves no new marker. Status warns when an existing marker's directory is unignored and names the setup command to fix it without overwriting the marker.

Once present, every `Edit` / `Write` / `MultiEdit` triggers a Codex review of the changed file. HIGH and MED concerns appear to Claude as a system reminder on the next turn, prefixed with `[codex-pair]` and the file path:

```
[codex-pair] src/billing/charge.ts

[HIGH] Monetary values are modeled as floating-point numbers
src/billing/charge.ts:12: `price` accepts arbitrary JS numbers for
money, which violates the stated requirement that currency uses
integer cents. Use integer minor units such as
`priceCents: z.number().int().nonnegative()`.
```

### When to enable it

Decide BEFORE you opt in; the hook consumes provider quota or incurs account charges per edit, and the value is highest on code where missed concerns have outsized blast radius. The decision is about **code characteristics**, not project domain: any project has both kinds of code, and codex-pair earns its keep wherever there's a category of "looks fine, runs wrong" failure mode.

| Use the hook (recall-first) | Stick with `/codex-review` only (precision-first) |
|---|---|
| Code with hidden invariants the model can't infer from one file | Routine PR review |
| Code where latent bugs justify per-edit quota use | Glue code, simple CRUD, refactors |
| Code evolving fast under written constraints (spec, protocol, ADR) | Cost-sensitive sessions |
| State coordination, concurrency, anything order-sensitive | One comprehensive report is enough |
| The "looks fine, runs wrong" failure mode would be expensive to catch later | |

## Slash commands

The `/codex-pair` suite is the human-facing dashboard and controls for the hook. The hook itself runs automatically once the marker exists; these commands are for setup, inspection, and toggling.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `/codex-pair` | Runs [setup](#setup) when needed, starts a catch-up pass for an active marker and shows status |
| `/codex-pair-pause` | Pause the hook for this project without removing the marker. Writes a `.codex-pair/state/paused` sentinel the hook checks on every edit and records the pause. Use to temporarily silence reviews (noisy refactor, docs-only work) and resume later |
| `/codex-pair-resume` | Remove the pause sentinel, clear the failure counter and record the resume. Starts a catch-up pass and re-enables per-edit review. No-op if no pause sentinel exists |
| `/codex-pair-ack <hash> "<reason>"` | Acknowledge a HIGH finding without fixing it (known trade-off or tracked in a ticket). The `<hash>` is the content hash shown alongside the finding when the Stop gate blocks. The reason is recorded as a concurrency-safe shard under `.codex-pair/state/acks/` with a timestamp; acknowledged findings are skipped by the gate until the file changes |

## The hook pipeline

codex-pair is implemented as five hooks working together, all dependency-free with zero workspace imports so they run from marketplace `git-subdir` installs that don't run `npm install`. The watch hook sends reviews through the broker when available and uses `codex exec --json` for direct reviews. Catch-up uses the same watch hook through the detached worker; the prompt drain delivers persisted verdicts.

| Hook | Trigger | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `codex-pair-watch` (PostToolUse) | After every `Edit` / `Write` / `MultiEdit` | If a `.codex-pair/context.md` marker exists from the edited file's directory up to the project root, the edit is queued for review with the marker's content as context. Edits are **debounced**: a burst within the 15s settle window coalesces into one review of the settled state, run by a detached worker. No marker means the hook exits silently after one `fs.access()` call: **zero Codex calls, zero cost** |
| `codex-pair-prompt-drain` (UserPromptSubmit) | On every user prompt | Drains queued codex-pair verdicts that finished mid-turn so they reach Claude without waiting for the next edit |
| `codex-pair-stop-gate` (Stop) | At turn end | Starts a catch-up pass in the background and drains queued verdicts. With `blockOn: HIGH` in the marker frontmatter (opt-in, default OFF), blocks turn-end while unaddressed HIGH findings or in-flight reviews remain. See [Stop gate](#stop-gate-opt-in) below |
| `codex-pair-session` (SessionStart) | At Claude session start | Announces or clears a pause, starts the broker when enabled and catches up after automatic resume |
| `codex-pair-session` (SessionEnd) | At Claude session end | Clears debounce state and tears down this session's broker |

By default HIGH and MED concerns are surfaced; LOW concerns and all timing/skip telemetry are logged to `.codex-pair/log.jsonl` alongside the marker file. Set `debounceMs: 0` in the marker frontmatter for synchronous per-edit review.

In the shared review hook scripts (Claude Code and Grok CLI), a reviewer reply that matches neither the JSON verdict contract nor the legacy `NONE` / `[HIGH]`/`[MED]`/`[LOW]` format is never recorded as "no concerns": it is logged with verdict `unparsed` (with a short excerpt of the reply), surfaced once as `codex-pair UNPARSED`, left out of the review cache, and counted towards the consecutive-failure auto-pause. Pi also requires a recognized review and records unrecognized responses as failed attempts.

### Catch-up review

On Claude Code, catch-up runs when `/codex-pair` finds or creates an active marker, on manual or automatic resume, and at turn end. Each pass reviews up to 10 files in sequence within one two-minute budget, using the same worker, cache, and file rules as per-edit review. Quota auto-pause ends the pass. The Stop hook starts the pass without waiting for a review. Set `catchUpOnStop: false` in `.codex-pair/context.md` frontmatter to skip the turn-end pass for that project.

A pass considers eligible dirty or untracked files in the marker's Git repository and any sibling repositories already registered in the session. It can pick up edits made through the shell, before activation, or during a pause. Shell writes committed before the pass, sibling repositories touched only through the shell, and deletions are outside its coverage. Catch-up also skips symlinks, symlinked path components beneath the marker directory, and files under another marker. No Bash hook is registered on Claude Code.

A retained successful review (`none`, `concerns`, or `cached`) counts when its content hash matches the current file and its review context is current, even after the cache expires. Failed attempts and debounce generations do not count. Losing the successful record to log rotation or changing the marker or resolved reviewer/model settings makes the file eligible again; a compatible cache hit can satisfy the new pass.

### Configuration knobs

| Env var | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `CODEX_PAIR_DISABLED` | unset | Set to `1` to bypass the hook entirely; beats marker file |
| `CODEX_PAIR_MAX_FILE_BYTES` | `20000` | Files larger than this many UTF-8 bytes get an adaptive **partial-view** review (header + git diff, or head+tail), not a full-content one. Still a Codex call; use `.codex-pair/ignore` to skip calls for excluded files |
| `ASK_CODEX_TIMEOUT_MS` | `800000` | Fallback review timeout in milliseconds; empty, non-numeric, non-positive, or infinite values use the default. Set `timeoutMs` in `.codex-pair/context.md` frontmatter to override it for this project. A debounced review retains the timeout resolved when its worker was scheduled, even if frontmatter changes during the settle window; the worker uses that timeout for its review process and in-flight lock. An enabled broker gets half the review budget, leaving the remainder for direct fallback |
| `ASK_CODEX_REASONING_EFFORT` | `high` | Codex pair reasoning effort; marker `reasoningEffort` takes precedence |
| `ASK_CODEX_BROKER` | disabled | Set to `1` to opt in to the broker unless the project sets `broker: false`; otherwise use per-edit `codex exec` |
| `ASK_CODEX_DEBOUNCE_MS` | `15000` | Settle window: an edit burst to one file coalesces into a single review of the settled state. `0` = synchronous per-edit review. Also settable per-marker via `debounceMs` frontmatter |
| `ASK_CODEX_DEBOUNCE_MAX_MS` | `60000` | Hard cap from a burst's first edit; forces a review even under a continuous edit stream. Frontmatter: `debounceMaxMs` |
| `CODEX_PAIR_QUOTA_PAUSE_TTL_MS` | `21600000` (6h) | Quota auto-pauses self-heal after this long; the next edit (or session start) retries a live review |
| `CODEX_PAIR_FAILURES_PAUSE_TTL_MS` | `86400000` (24h) | Failure auto-pauses self-heal after this long, or immediately when the plugin version changed since the pause |

For Codex reviews through the shared Claude Code/Grok hook, marker frontmatter `model` and `fallbackModel` override `ASK_CODEX_MODEL` and `ASK_CODEX_FALLBACK_MODEL`, then `codex-pair-defaults.json`. `reasoningEffort` follows the same precedence: marker, `ASK_CODEX_REASONING_EFFORT`, defaults file, then `high`. Supported effort values are `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max` and `ultra`; invalid values fall through. The resolved effort applies to direct and broker calls, including retries and quota fallback, and changing it invalidates the review cache. For the pinned Claude reviewer and its timeout, see [Grok CLI](#grok-cli). Pi's separate implementation is unchanged.

```yaml
---
model: gpt-6.2-sol
reasoningEffort: xhigh
blockOn: false
---
```

The broker is opt-in because it links your `auth.json`; a token refresh can rewrite that shared file, and a safer credential strategy has not been established. Set `ASK_CODEX_BROKER=1` to enable it. It runs `codex app-server` in a private temporary Codex home without user hooks, rules, or MCP configuration and with the built-in apps connector disabled. Without an `auth.json` (keyring or environment-key setups) the broker does not start. To disable it for one project, put `broker: false` in `.codex-pair/context.md` frontmatter. `ASK_CODEX_BROKER=0` also disables it.

Startup, transport, health, and protocol failures use the per-edit `codex exec` path. A quota error from the broker goes straight to the fallback model, and a transient provider error (502/503/504, connection resets) gets one direct retry. A broker turn gets half the review timeout, leaving the remaining time for its first direct fallback attempt; each later transient retry or fallback-model attempt gets only the time left after the broker turn. The broker's socket path is inside its private home, so deep project paths do not matter; Codex 0.156.1 makes that path a symlink to a socket in its shared per-user daemon directory, and teardown removes only the symlink; a broker recovered from an interrupted start is SIGKILLed, so its socket file stays in that daemon directory. A recorded broker is only signaled or reused while its process is still `codex app-server` on the recorded socket; a dead process, an expired 24-hour owner lease, or a broker bound to a different credential home is replaced on the next opted-in SessionStart. If `ps` cannot verify a recorded broker, SessionStart leaves its descriptor and private home intact and starts no replacement; the next SessionStart or SessionEnd can check again. An opted-in session without its own `auth.json` never stops another session's healthy broker. A SessionStart killed mid-start is recovered by the next one when `ps` can check for its orphan. An opted-out SessionStart leaves another session's healthy broker running and retires it only if the broker's own credential source is absent. A broker left running after a missed SessionEnd can therefore remain until an opted-in SessionStart recovers it, its owner ends, or its credential source disappears; there is no global orphan reaper. Overlapping Claude sessions in one project share one broker: when the session that started it ends, the others review through `codex exec` until a new session starts one.

Cold start measured under one second and warm reviews were no faster. The hooks, the broker, and every helper script are written in TypeScript and ship as generated JavaScript, so they run from a marketplace checkout or an npm install without a build step; they support Node 24 (the current LTS) or newer.

### Auto-pause is self-healing

When the hook pauses itself (provider quota exhausted, or 3 consecutive review failures), the pause no longer requires a manual `/codex-pair-resume` to ever end:

- **At session start** a paused project announces itself: a reminder if the pause is still fresh, or an automatic resume if it has expired. No more silently-dead pairing.
- **On any edit** an expired auto-pause resumes in place and that edit gets reviewed; if the provider is still broken, the review fails and the hook re-pauses cleanly.
- **Plugin updates heal failure-pauses immediately**: the pause sentinel records the plugin version that wrote it, and a version change is treated as "the cause was plausibly fixed".
- **Manual pauses are untouched**: `/codex-pair-pause` still only ever resumes via `/codex-pair-resume`.

### Cost characteristics

- Usage varies by the selected model, reasoning effort, and workload; see [Account costs](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/operation/costs#account-costs).
- Files over the size cap fall back to an adaptive partial-view review (header + git diff against HEAD, OR head + tail)
- `node_modules/`, `dist/`, lockfiles, fonts, archives, sourcemaps, snapshots, minified assets skipped automatically
- The content-hash cache skips unchanged review inputs; changing reasoning effort causes a cache miss.

For typical opted-in projects (small surface where review depth matters), the cost is acceptable. For routine refactor work across a whole repo, leave the marker file out and use `/codex-review` on demand instead.

### Disable it

| Goal | How |
|---|---|
| Temporarily for this project | `/codex-pair-pause` (resume with `/codex-pair-resume`) |
| Permanently for this project | `rm -rf .codex-pair/` |
| Just this Claude Code session | `/plugin disable ask-llm` |
| Just this command | `CODEX_PAIR_DISABLED=1 <command>` |

## Stop gate (opt-in)

**Default:** OFF. You must explicitly opt in.

**Trigger:** At the end of every Claude turn (`Stop` event).

**Action:** If unaddressed HIGH codex-pair findings remain in `.codex-pair/log.jsonl`, the hook blocks turn-end and surfaces those findings, forcing them to be addressed before the session continues.

> **Why opt-in?** Blocking turn-end is disruptive for some workflows, so blocking defaults OFF. The gate decides from persisted findings and in-flight state. [Catch-up review](#catch-up-review) runs independently of `blockOn`; disable its turn-end pass separately with `catchUpOnStop`.

### Enable it

Add a `blockOn` key to your `.codex-pair/context.md` YAML frontmatter:

```markdown
---
blockOn: HIGH
---

# .codex-pair/context.md

This is a payment-processing service. All currency calculations must
use integer cents internally (floating-point loses precision on every
charge).

[Your domain context here...]
```

Once enabled, the hook checks at turn-end whether any HIGH findings in `log.jsonl` are unacknowledged and unresolved. It reconciles against present reality before blocking:

- **File deleted or renamed** → finding skipped (no longer relevant)
- **File clean vs HEAD** (`git status --porcelain=v1 -z --untracked-files=all`) → finding skipped (reverted or branch-switched away); new files inside untracked directories remain eligible to block, including files in nested git repositories reported as `?? dir/`, except files ignored by the outer repository's `.gitignore`
- **Latest review of the content on disk is indeterminate** (`error`/`retried`/`broker_fallback`) → fail-open, finding skipped (don't block on a stale HIGH from before a transient error). Skip entries have no content hash and do not displace the last review.
- **No review matches the content on disk** → finding skipped. A queued settled edit gets its own review; edits outside Claude can be picked up by [catch-up](#catch-up-review). The gate uses the latest matching review even if a review of older content finished afterward, including when that review was logged under another path to the same file (such as `/var` and `/private/var` on macOS).

### In-flight reviews block too

With the default 15s debounce plus model review latency, a review is often still running when the turn ends; the log alone can't see it. When `blockOn: HIGH` is set, the gate also blocks (once per turn) while any review for a recent edit is still in flight (a settling debounce window, including a worker waiting for an earlier review of the same file, or a running Codex call), telling Claude to wait for the verdict before finishing. The `stop_hook_active` loop guard means a turn is never blocked twice for the same reason.

### Queued verdicts drain at turn-end

Debounced verdicts that finished mid-turn used to wait for the *next* edit or user prompt to surface. The Stop hook drains them at turn-end, no `blockOn` opt-in required: as additional context when nothing blocks, or folded into the block message when it does. A queued verdict surfaces only while the file still holds the content it reviewed; a verdict for content that has since changed is dropped. The Stop and user-prompt hooks drain both the working directory's marker and sibling repositories registered by this session's edit hooks. Cross-repository verdicts (cwd in repo A, edit in repo B) can therefore surface at turn-end or on the next user prompt without switching cwd. Each marker's `blockOn` setting controls blocking for that repository. Without a session ID, only the working directory's marker is available.

### Fail-open behavior

Any error in the stop-gate hook (missing log, parse error, git unavailable) warns to stderr and exits 0; the turn is **never** blocked due to a hook bug. This is intentional: a gate that blocks turns on its own fault is worse than no gate.

## Troubleshooting and verification

### Inspecting log activity: the `codex-pair-log` CLI

Shipped alongside the hook at `packages/llm-mcp/scripts/codex-pair-log.mjs`. Log and status commands walk up from cwd to find the marker (same gate as the hook), then read the sibling `.codex-pair/log.jsonl`. Useful for "is the hook actually running" diagnostics and for forensic analysis of what's been reviewed. The `setup` subcommand can run before a marker exists; see [Setup](#setup).

```bash
# Read-only status: resolved configuration, disable/pause state, last five reviews
node packages/llm-mcp/scripts/codex-pair-log.mjs --status

# Default: last 10 entries
node packages/llm-mcp/scripts/codex-pair-log.mjs

# Aggregate stats: verdict breakdown, top 5 files, cache hit rate, fallback frequency
node packages/llm-mcp/scripts/codex-pair-log.mjs --summary

# Filter to one file's history (including reviews logged through another path to the same file)
node packages/llm-mcp/scripts/codex-pair-log.mjs --file src/billing/charge.ts

# Only the last 24 hours
node packages/llm-mcp/scripts/codex-pair-log.mjs --since 24h --latest 50

# Pairing evidence for the last 24 hours
node packages/llm-mcp/scripts/codex-pair-log.mjs --report --since 24h
node packages/llm-mcp/scripts/codex-pair-log.mjs --report --since 24h --json
```

`--report` uses the repository marker found from the current directory. By default it covers all retained log entries, including Pi reviews. With `--since`, review counts, findings and attributions use the selected window, and the report includes pause windows that overlap it. **HIGH blocking now** uses the full retained log and the current Stop gate's rules, including marker opt-in, the file's dirty state and current content, and acknowledgements. Other unacknowledged HIGHs are listed separately.

The report counts actual successful reviews and cache hits separately. A finding hash counts once at its highest observed severity, and later appearances, including cache hits, count as repeats. The report includes acknowledgement reasons and findings no longer reported on the latest review of their file. Missing historical attribution is shown as `unknown`. When retained reviews lack finding identities, finding counts and lists describe only known evidence: the human output labels them `known (partial)`, and JSON sets `findingsComplete: false`. This qualification covers unique findings by severity, repeats, acknowledgements, other unacknowledged HIGHs, and findings no longer reported on the latest review of their file; current gate blockers remain a separate exact result. Claude's effort also appears as `unknown` because pairing does not set or observe it. New Pi reviews report their reviewer, model and effort; historical Pi reviews may show `unknown`. Pi's pause/resume handlers do not yet record structured events. Copy the first line into a pull request description or closing status. The remaining lines contain details, which are also available as JSON.

The current coverage section lists eligible dirty files as pending, failed, or not started. Files beyond a pass's time or file limit appear by name. In JSON, the `unreviewedFiles` array identifies each file by its marker directory and relative path. This section uses the full retained log and can include registered sibling repositories when the session ID is available. `--since` only limits the historical metrics.

If coverage cannot be determined because Git scanning, marker reading, or reviewer configuration fails in the project or a registered sibling, `--report` exits with an error instead of returning empty coverage. A disappeared sibling marker is skipped. In a non-Git project, historical metrics remain available, with no files in Git coverage.

From the project directory, the same CLI accepts `pause` and `resume` to change the sentinel and record transitions. Use `ack <hash>` with a non-empty reason on stdin to acknowledge a finding. For example, pipe `printf '%s\n' 'Accepted pending follow-up'` to `node packages/llm-mcp/scripts/codex-pair-log.mjs ack fc69d46835dfd2ab`.

`--status` reads the same resolver as the hook and works before any review is logged; a missing marker produces an error. It reports `disabled (CODEX_PAIR_DISABLED=1)`, `paused (manual|quota|failures)` or `active`. An invalid or same-family reviewer also reports `disabled` with the refusal reason, unless the disable switch or a pause takes precedence. For valid configuration it shows the reviewer, model, fallback, effort, threshold, timeout, file-size limit, debounce settings and `Guards turn end on: HIGH` or `nothing`. Claude review labels fallback and effort as unused.

It observes pause state without clearing expired auto-pauses or starting a reviewer. These are the current process's resolved settings; run it with the hook's environment. For Grok CLI, prefix the command with `CODEX_PAIR_HOST=grok` so reviewer selection uses the Grok writer family. Active means the marker is enabled and unpaused, not proof that a host registered or ran its hook; recent log entries provide that evidence. The Claude Code skill uses the `start` subcommand to schedule catch-up before showing the same status.

Output shape (one line per log entry):

```
2026-05-18T15:11:02.341Z  none          /project/src/billing/charge.ts        0H/0M/0L    6.2s
2026-05-18T15:11:14.892Z  concerns      /project/src/billing/charge.ts        1H/0M/0L    8.7s
2026-05-18T15:11:18.001Z  cached        /project/src/billing/charge.ts        1H/0M/0L    3ms
```

Zero workspace imports; runs on a marketplace install with no `node_modules`.

### If the hook isn't firing automatically: the project-settings workaround (issue #74)

Some Claude Code installations don't auto-invoke plugin-declared PostToolUse hooks even though the plugin is correctly installed and `/reload-plugins` reports the hook count. This appears to be a Claude Code platform issue with the plugin-hook dispatch path; see [issue #74](https://github.com/Lykhoyda/ask-llm/issues/74) for the full diagnostic chain. The hook script itself works perfectly when invoked manually or when registered via a `~/.claude/settings.json` / `.claude/settings.local.json` `hooks` block.

**Quick diagnostic**: edit any file under your marker-anchored project. If `.codex-pair/log.jsonl` mtime doesn't advance within ~60s, you're hitting the dispatch bug.

**Workaround**: add a `hooks.PostToolUse` block to your **project-local** `.claude/settings.local.json` (per-developer; gitignored by convention) that invokes the hook script directly, bypassing the plugin-dispatch path. Pick the command form that matches your use case:

#### Form A: Plugin maintainer (you're working on the ask-llm repo itself)

Point at the local repo source via `$PWD` so the path resolves to whatever directory Claude Code was launched in (the workspace root). Always reflects your current branch's working tree: no manual update on version bumps, no hardcoded absolute paths to maintain, and the same config works for every contributor regardless of where they cloned the repo:

```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PostToolUse": [
      {
        "matcher": "Edit|Write|MultiEdit",
        "hooks": [
          {
            "type": "command",
            "command": "sh -c 'node \"$PWD/packages/llm-mcp/scripts/codex-pair-watch.mjs\"'"
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Caveats:
- Requires launching Claude Code from the repo root (so `$PWD` resolves there). If you launch from a parent directory the hook silently fails; easy to spot via `node packages/llm-mcp/scripts/codex-pair-log.mjs --latest`.
- Requires a POSIX shell (`sh`) in `PATH`, which macOS and Linux have natively.

#### Form B: Plugin user (you installed via marketplace)

Resolve the highest semver-sorted version from the cache at invocation time with Node's cross-platform numeric sort, so the workaround keeps working across plugin updates without relying on GNU-only `sort -V`:

```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PostToolUse": [
      {
        "matcher": "Edit|Write|MultiEdit",
        "hooks": [
          {
            "type": "command",
            "command": "node -e \"try { const fs=require('fs'),cp=require('child_process'),p=process.env.HOME+'/.claude/plugins/cache/ask-llm-plugins/ask-llm'; const v=fs.readdirSync(p).sort((a,b)=>a.localeCompare(b,undefined,{numeric:true})).at(-1); if(v) process.exitCode=cp.spawnSync(process.execPath,[p+'/'+v+'/scripts/codex-pair-watch.mjs'],{stdio:'inherit'}).status??0; } catch {}\""
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

The Node command picks the highest numeric semver directory under the cache and passes the hook payload through inherited stdin. It is a silent no-op if no install is present.

#### After either form

Fully quit and restart Claude Code to pick up the new hook config; `/reload-plugins` refreshes plugin files but does not re-register hooks in the current session. After restarting, the next Edit/Write/MultiEdit should fire the hook automatically. Verify with `node <plugin-path>/scripts/codex-pair-log.mjs --latest` or a new `.codex-pair/log.jsonl` entry (typical wall clock 5-30s per call).

Note: this workaround is per-developer (project-local) and gitignored. Once Claude Code's plugin-hook dispatch is fixed upstream, you can remove the `hooks` block and rely on the plugin's own registration again.

### Grok pair

Source: https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/advanced/grok-pair.html

Claude Code's `/grok-pair` selects one immutable Grok route: `cursor-agent` (preferred when configured with an exact Grok-family ID from `agent --list-models`), `xai-api`, or `grok-cli`. Before provider work it shows provider, harness, exact model, reasoning semantics, bounded files/include directories, session support, and cost boundary for consent. Claude remains the editor; Grok feedback is relayed and verified at each checkpoint. Cancellation, partial failure, and final attribution are explicit; Auto, model rewriting, and provider/harness fallback are forbidden.

```text
/grok-pair route=cursor-agent model=grok-4.7-high include=packages/api review this change
/grok-pair route=xai-api model=grok-4.7 effort=xhigh review this change
```

On Claude Code, setup registers the connection for Cursor and direct Grok tools; the Claude adapter itself bundles only Codex. The unified `ask-llm` tool is used only with provider, harness, exact model, and effort pinned. When Cursor itself hosts `/grok-pair`, it avoids recursive Cursor invocation and offers only explicit API/CLI routes through `ask-grok` or that fully pinned unified form; missing tools produce `.cursor/mcp.json` plus Cursor Tools & MCP reload guidance, never Claude-only setup commands.

On Pi this workflow refuses because a dedicated Grok consent/lifecycle adapter is not available. Setup leaves pairing off on every host. See [Cursor host notes](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/compatibility/cursor#grok-pair-route-safety) and [costs](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/operation/costs).

### Manual MCP configuration

Source: https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/advanced/manual-configuration.html

MCP is the connection protocol used by most hosts. Pi uses a native extension instead; see [Pi host notes](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/compatibility/pi). Primary onboarding uses [setup](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/start/install), which registers a durable installed path.

Use manual configuration only when setup prints guidance (it always does for Codex), your host requires project scope, or your client is outside the supported host list. Start with the exact entry setup prints and keep unrelated servers intact. The installed executable is `ask-llm-mcp`; use `command -v ask-llm-mcp` to find its absolute path.

## JSON clients

For a client that accepts `mcpServers`, replace the placeholder with that absolute path:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "ask-llm": {
      "command": "/absolute/path/to/ask-llm-mcp",
      "args": []
    }
  }
}
```

Cursor uses `~/.cursor/mcp.json` at user scope or `.cursor/mcp.json` in a project; Claude Desktop uses its `claude_desktop_config.json`. Other hosts have different schemas: do not copy this JSON into Pi, OpenCode or a TOML client. Setup prints the host-specific form and manual steps.

## Command hosts

Pass the absolute executable path to the host's registration command:

```bash
claude mcp add --scope user ask-llm -- /absolute/path/to/ask-llm-mcp
codex mcp add ask-llm -- /absolute/path/to/ask-llm-mcp
```

For a default global install, the path is `"$(npm prefix -g)/bin/ask-llm-mcp"`, which is what setup prints. Inspect both user and project configuration before adding or changing a Codex entry; preserve filters and custom options. Restart the host after registration. Run `ask-llm doctor`, then request a [first review](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/start/first-review); a registration check alone is not a successful provider call.

Legacy cache-based registrations and marketplace commands are retained in [Migration](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/reference/migration#earlier-installation-recipes). See [CLI](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/reference/cli) and [authentication](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/operation/authentication) for diagnostics and credentials.

## Codex tool timeout

After the manual `codex mcp add` command, edit the existing `ask-llm` server table in `~/.codex/config.toml` (or `$CODEX_HOME/config.toml`). Preserve its command, arguments, environment and tool filters, and merge this setting into that table rather than appending a duplicate table:

```toml
[mcp_servers.ask-llm]
tool_timeout_sec = 2460
```

`ask-llm setup --host codex` prints this setting alongside the registration command; setup does not write Codex configuration. The 2,460-second allowance is derived from the largest shared default per-attempt limit (800 seconds) × the maximum three provider attempts + 60 seconds for probes and response overhead. Codex's longest ladder is the optional preferred model, the default model, then the quota fallback. Concurrent `multi-llm` participants share the same host deadline.

If you raise `GMCPT_TIMEOUT_MS` or a provider-specific limit (`ASK_CODEX_TIMEOUT_MS`, `ASK_CLAUDE_TIMEOUT_MS`, `ASK_GEMINI_TIMEOUT_MS`, `ASK_GROK_TIMEOUT_MS`, `ASK_CURSOR_TIMEOUT_MS`, `ASK_OLLAMA_TIMEOUT_MS` or `ASK_ANTIGRAVITY_TIMEOUT_MS`) in the server environment, raise the host setting too: `tool_timeout_sec >= ceil(largest configured per-attempt limit in ms * 3 / 1000) + 60`. For example, a 1,200,000 ms limit needs at least 3,660 seconds. Restart Codex after editing configuration, and inspect project overrides that may replace the user setting.

[Codex documents a 60-second default](https://developers.openai.com/codex/mcp). A 75-second ask-llm call on Codex CLI 0.167.0 completed with no explicit host timeout while receiving progress every 25 seconds. That observation does not establish the behavior of a silent call or other Codex versions; configure the full allowance explicitly.

### Enterprise environments / Gemini

Source: https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/advanced/enterprise-gemini.html

Gemini CLI requires an existing, eligible Code Assist Standard or Enterprise seat. Check your organisation's data-transfer policy before sending project material. See the [Gemini provider reference](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/providers/gemini) for account eligibility and failure behavior.

Ask LLM normally supplies Gemini workspace-trust settings for the current directory. Set `ASK_GEMINI_REQUIRE_WORKSPACE_TRUST=1` to require explicit workspace trust instead; untrusted directories then block. User-scope Gemini registrations load only in trusted folders. See [environment variables](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/reference/environment-variables).

Gemini CLI ships a sandboxed code-execution environment that lets the model write and run code in an isolated context. This is a **Gemini CLI feature**, not a feature of the MCP server.

::: tip Gemini CLI sandbox
Gemini CLI sandbox mode requires the same [account eligibility](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/providers/gemini) as other Gemini CLI calls.
:::

## Why isn't there a `sandbox` parameter on `ask-gemini` anymore?

The `ask-gemini` MCP tool schema was simplified from 8 parameters to 2 (`prompt` + `model`) for token efficiency and to reduce LLM-induced parameter hallucinations. The `sandbox` parameter was one of the casualties; it's a niche feature that most users don't need, and exposing it added noise to every Claude/Codex/Cursor instance loading the tool definition.

The underlying executor still supports sandbox mode programmatically; only the MCP-facing schema dropped it.

## How to use sandbox mode today

If you need Gemini's sandbox, run `gemini` directly from your terminal with the `-s` flag:

```bash
gemini -s -p "Write a Python script that sorts a list and run it"
```

Inside Claude Code, you can dispatch this via Bash:

```text
Run this in bash: gemini -s -p "Write and execute a Python script that validates this JSON: ..."
```

The plugin's `ask-gemini-run` binary (a small node wrapper) also passes through to the executor; you can adapt it if you want a programmatic path.

## When you'd actually want sandbox mode

- Testing snippets the model just generated (write + execute in one round-trip)
- Quick proof-of-concepts where you want runtime evidence, not just code
- Learning: see code execute with real output

For most workflows (review, analysis, refactor suggestions), sandbox is unnecessary and the simpler `ask-gemini` / `ask-llm` MCP tools are the right call.

## Limitations

Sandbox capabilities depend on your Gemini CLI version and Gemini account. See the [Gemini CLI documentation](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli) for current sandbox features and constraints.

## Resources

### Troubleshooting

Source: https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/resources/troubleshooting.html

> **Run the doctor first.** `ask-llm doctor` checks Node version, PATH, every provider CLI's presence + version, and env vars. It works even when MCP can't start. Follow the failed-check remediation for your selected assistant and reviewer. Warnings about providers you do not use do not require installing them or adding API keys.

```bash
ask-llm doctor                       # human-readable
ask-llm doctor --json                # established full JSON, exit 1 on error
ask-llm doctor --format toon         # bounded, versioned agent-facing TOON pilot
ask-llm doctor --format toon --full  # full TOON escape hatch
```

After a global install, use `ask-llm doctor` for host and provider states. The optional `--live` check may spend provider quota; see [Diagnostics / doctor](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/operation/diagnostics) for the state meanings and output formats.




## Installation Issues

### "Command not found: gemini" / "codex" / "ollama"

Provider CLI is not installed or not on PATH

A provider CLI is missing or not on PATH. Install:

```bash
# Gemini
npm install -g @google/gemini-cli

# Codex
npm install -g @openai/codex
# then follow the codex CLI's auth instructions

# Ollama (https://ollama.com)
ollama pull qwen3.8:27b
```

Verify:

```bash
gemini --version    # or: which gemini
codex --version
ollama list
```

If `ask-llm doctor` reports a CLI as "not found on PATH" but `which <cli>` works in your terminal, the issue is PATH inheritance; see the next entry.




### "PATH issue": CLI works in terminal but MCP server says "not found"

macOS GUI apps don't inherit your shell PATH

macOS GUI applications (Claude Desktop, Cursor, etc.) don't source `.zshrc` / `.bashrc`, so nvm / Homebrew / Volta paths aren't visible to the MCP server. Ask LLM resolves this automatically by extracting the real PATH from your login shell at startup.

If it's still failing:

1. Confirm `ask-llm doctor` shows a non-empty `Resolved PATH` with the CLI's directory in it.
2. If it doesn't, set `ASK_LLM_PATH` explicitly in your MCP client's env config:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "ask-llm": {
      "command": "/absolute/path/to/ask-llm-mcp",
      "args": [],
      "env": {
        "ASK_LLM_PATH": "/usr/local/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:$HOME/.nvm/versions/node/v24.0.0/bin"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

3. Restart your MCP client completely (not just reload).




### MCP server not responding (Claude Desktop cannot connect)

Server fails to start or connection drops

**Step-by-step:**

1. **Check Node.js version**: must be ≥ v24:
   ```bash
   node --version
   ```
2. **Run the doctor** to identify what's missing:
   ```bash
   ask-llm doctor
   ```
3. **Verify Claude Desktop config syntax**: use a JSON validator. Common bugs: trailing commas, missing brackets.
4. **Restart Claude Desktop completely**:
   - Quit (Cmd+Q on Mac), wait 5s, reopen.
   - Just reloading the window is not enough.
5. **Check logs** for the actual error:
   - macOS: `~/Library/Logs/Claude/mcp-server-*.log`
   - Linux: `~/.config/claude/logs/`




### EUNSUPPORTEDPROTOCOL workspace:* in an earlier npx registration

An earlier cached installation can fail before the server starts

Earlier cache-based registrations can contain stale package metadata. Use [Migration](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/reference/migration) to replace a verified old entry with the durable installed path. Preserve customised environment variables and filters first. Primary onboarding does not depend on an npx server cache.




## Connection & Auth

### "Authentication failed" / "401 Unauthorized"

Provider CLI isn't authenticated

Each provider has its own auth flow:

- **Gemini:** Sign in with the account assigned to your [existing, eligible Code Assist Standard or Enterprise seat](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/providers/gemini). Individual access ended June 18, 2026. If you choose Antigravity through Ask LLM, check [Google's consumer-plan terms and the local prerequisites](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/providers/antigravity).
- **Codex**: follow `codex` CLI's auth instructions (varies by version)
- **Ollama**: no auth needed; Ollama just needs to be running locally

Verify each CLI works directly before blaming the MCP server:

```bash
gemini "Hello"
codex exec --skip-git-repo-check "Hello"
curl http://localhost:11434/api/tags    # Ollama
```




### Quota / rate limit errors (Gemini RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, Codex 429)

Provider quota exhausted

**The executor handles this automatically**: Gemini falls back from `gemini-4-argon` to `gemini-3.8-flash`, and Codex falls back from `gpt-6.2-sol` to `gpt-6.1-terra`. You'll see `usage.fellBack: true` in the structured response.

If both Pro and Flash (or both GPT-6.2 Sol and Terra) hit quota, the call fails with both errors surfaced. Wait for the quota window to reset, or:

- Switch to a different provider for the meantime: `Use ask-llm with provider codex ...` instead of Gemini
- Use Ollama locally: `Use ask-llm with provider ollama ...`




### "Command timed out after Xs"

Provider call exceeded the per-provider wall-clock timeout

Defaults differ by provider: **codex 800s** (reasoning models routinely take 5–10 min on substantive prompts), **gemini 210s** (stream-json emits tokens incrementally, usually fast enough). Resolution ladder: per-provider env var > `GMCPT_TIMEOUT_MS` > provider default.

For long analyses (large diffs, deep Codex reasoning):

1. **Override codex's timeout** when only codex is slow:
   ```json
   { "env": { "ASK_CODEX_TIMEOUT_MS": "1200000" } }   // 20 minutes
   ```

2. **Override gemini's timeout** independently:
   ```json
   { "env": { "ASK_GEMINI_TIMEOUT_MS": "600000" } }   // 10 minutes
   ```

3. **Lift both at once** with the global override (kept for backward compatibility):
   ```json
   { "env": { "GMCPT_TIMEOUT_MS": "1200000" } }       // applies to gemini AND codex
   ```

4. **For multi-provider review skills** (`/multi-review`, `/brainstorm`), large diffs may take 5–15 min; use the diff size policy in those skills (filter docs/binaries, truncate above 150KB) to keep them tractable.

5. **For very large prompts**, consider splitting the work or using `ask-gemini` with `includeDirs` instead of one giant prompt.

Note: Claude Desktop has its own client-side timeout (~4 min on some setups) that runs independently of the server. Raising server-side timeouts past that gives the REPL and direct executor calls more headroom but won't help Claude Desktop sessions specifically.

To check the resolved per-provider timeouts on your machine, run `ask-llm:diagnose`; its `Timeouts:` line shows the effective values for both codex and gemini.




## Tool & API Issues

### "Provider X is not available" / tool call rejects provider

The orchestrator didn't detect the provider at startup

Ask LLM detects available providers at startup. If a provider you expected isn't there:

1. Run `ask-llm doctor` to see what it detects.
2. The most common cause is PATH not finding the provider CLI; see the PATH issue entry above.
3. For Ollama specifically, it must be **running** at `http://localhost:11434` (or wherever `OLLAMA_HOST` points). Not just installed.
4. Restart your MCP client to re-detect providers.




### "Sub-agent silently produces 0-byte output" / brainstorm coordinator hang

Provider process killed by sub-agent lifecycle

This is a known bug class: Claude Code sub-agents can't own background processes that outlive their turn, so `(cmd &) && wait` patterns or `run_in_background: true` on dispatch calls cause processes to be SIGKILLed silently.

The brainstorm-coordinator agent uses the correct pattern (single foreground blocking Bash with direct backgrounding + per-PID wait + `timeout: 600000`). If you're seeing this in custom skills you're writing, follow the same pattern; see the agent prompt in `packages/llm-mcp/agents/brainstorm-coordinator.md` for the canonical template.




## Model & Response Issues

### Response gets cut off mid-stream

MCP message size limits or executor timeout

For Gemini, large responses are chunked automatically; Claude can call `fetch-chunk` to retrieve subsequent chunks from the cached response.

For Codex / Ollama, very large responses can hit the MCP message limit. Workarounds:

- Ask for shorter responses ("3 bullets max", "1-paragraph summary")
- Split the work; run the prompt twice with narrower scope
- Use the REPL where output streams directly to stdout without MCP message size limits




## Plugin Issues

### Plugin slash commands not appearing in Claude Code

Plugin not installed or not loaded

Verify the plugin is installed and active:

```text
/plugin list
```

If `ask-llm` is missing, run `ask-llm setup --host claude`, follow its guidance, and fully restart Claude Code. Inspect `/mcp` after restart. The Claude adapter bundles Codex; setup also connects the user-scoped server for other providers.

If the registration is present but disconnected, run `ask-llm doctor`. A missing registration, disconnected service, and an older schema have different remediation. The review workflow discloses any CLI fallback. Legacy installation commands are retained in [Migration](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/reference/migration#earlier-installation-recipes).




## Debug Mode

Enable verbose logging:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "ask-llm": {
      "command": "/absolute/path/to/ask-llm-mcp",
      "args": [],
      "env": {
        "GMCPT_LOG_LEVEL": "debug"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Logs go to stderr. Claude Desktop captures them in:

- macOS: `~/Library/Logs/Claude/mcp-server-*.log`
- Linux: `~/.config/claude/logs/`

## Getting Help

1. **Run the doctor first**: `ask-llm doctor`
2. Check [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/Lykhoyda/ask-llm/issues) for similar reports
3. Open a new issue with: doctor output, your client (Claude Code/Desktop/Cursor/etc.), Node version, OS, and what you ran
4. Ask in [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/Lykhoyda/ask-llm/discussions) for usage questions

### Frequently asked questions

Source: https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/resources/faq.html

## What is Ask LLM?

Second opinions for coding agents. Get a second opinion on your code or plan, inside your coding assistant, using the model subscriptions you already have. It is for individual developers and small teams who already use a coding assistant and another model account.

## Do I need every provider?

No. Install and sign in to the provider you want to consult; Ask LLM configures its connection to your host. You need Node.js 24+ on Linux or macOS. Start at [Install](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/start/install).

## Which package should I choose?

There is one install line on [Install](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/start/install). Earlier installations have a [migration guide](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/reference/migration), rather than a separate onboarding path.

## What does a review cost?

Calls consume the selected account's quota or billing. Subscription-backed routes need no separate model API key. Grok's xAI API is an explicit metered option requiring a key; Grok Build and Cursor follow their plans. Ollama uses local compute. See [Costs and fallbacks](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/operation/costs).

## Can Codex ask Claude?

Yes. Claude is available from Codex and other hosts. It is suppressed inside Claude Code because nested Claude sessions are unsupported. Claude consultations use Read, Glob and Grep; your host applies changes.

## Does model agreement prove correctness?

No. Validate claims against source, tests and requirements. [Compare answers](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/workflows/compare-answers) preserves raw responses, while [review workflows](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/workflows/review-changes) check candidate findings against source.

## Which hosts work?

See [Hosts](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/compatibility/hosts). Claude Desktop is tools only. Pi uses native tools and needs no MCP config. Antigravity has a manual workflow-copy step. In Codex, setup prints the registration command for you to run after checking existing entries; OpenCode registration is verified with fixtures only.

## Why is Gemini restricted?

The provider requires an eligible Code Assist Standard/Enterprise seat. See [Enterprise environments / Gemini](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/advanced/enterprise-gemini) and the [provider reference](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/providers/gemini). Ask LLM cannot grant provider eligibility.

## Where does my code go?

To the provider you select, under its policies. Local Ollama inference stays on your local endpoint. Ask LLM sends no telemetry. Host conversations, provider sessions and opt-in pairing state have separate storage; see [Data flow](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/operation/data-flow).

## How do follow-up questions work?

See [Tools and schemas](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/reference/tools#sessions) for session-capable providers, first-call requirements and follow-up costs, and [Antigravity sessions](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/providers/antigravity#sessions) for its reset behavior.

## What is Gemini's @ file syntax?

The Gemini CLI interprets `@file.ts`, `@src/` and globs as file context. Other providers need relevant code in the prompt or their supported include-directory mechanism. Ask your assistant to bound the context.

## What should I check when a call fails?

Run `ask-llm doctor`. It distinguishes installation, registration, authentication, permission and optional live exercise. Healthy registration alone does not prove a provider call succeeds. See [Troubleshooting](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/resources/troubleshooting).

## Can I use Ask LLM in automation?

The product is designed for interactive review. The [CLI reference](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/reference/cli) documents the existing machine protocol and scripting flags. Check account eligibility and data policy before automating provider calls.

## More questions
